payload.title: Automate the non-trustworthy-origin browser leg for the cookie-borne-read same-origin proof

payload.description:
## Context

SH-319 fixed a real defect: `named_token_ok`'s cookie-borne-read gate required `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, a header browsers never send on a non-potentially-trustworthy origin (plain-http on a tailnet hostname or LAN IP, per the Fetch Metadata spec). The fix layers in `X-Storyhook` (primary, closes the whole class) and a `Referer`-vs-`Host` fallback for `EventSource` alone.

`docs/spec/dashboard-authorization.md`'s SH-255 "As built" section already flagged this exact gap before SH-319: *"Browser storage and Sec-Fetch-Site behavior are still unmeasured by any automated suite... This is the merge gate SH-255 has not yet cleared."* SH-319 proved the fix two ways — comprehensive Rust socket-level tests (`tests/token_exchange.rs`) matching the real HTTP contract header-for-header, and live manual verification with a real Chromium (via Playwright MCP) against this machine's actual bound tailnet address, reproducing the exact failure and confirming the fix across reload, new tab, and daemon restart. Neither is a repeatable CI leg.

## Problem

Automating the non-trustworthy-origin browser leg in `e2e/` turns out to need a *second, isolated* daemon, not a config tweak to the existing one. Investigated and rejected during SH-319:

- Getting Chromium to treat an origin as non-potentially-trustworthy needs a real non-loopback-looking hostname — `--host-resolver-rules="MAP storyhook.e2e.test 127.0.0.1"` is the standard technique (Chromium's own web-platform-tests use it), which is fine and hermetic on its own.
- But `mutation_guard_ok`'s `host_is_trusted` needs that hostname in the daemon's trusted-hosts allowlist, and the only lever for that is `STORYHOOK_WEB_TRUSTED_HOSTS` — which flips `TrustedHosts::behind_a_proxy()` true.
- `behind_a_proxy()` true makes `local_request` (`src/api/http.rs`) return `None` for *every* caller, including a genuine loopback one — it's the SH-250-era "a reverse proxy means loopback no longer means this machine" signal.
- `local_request` is what gates `story web open`'s coupon-arming route (`ARM_PATH`, `src/api/handoff.rs`), which `e2e/specs/handoff.spec.ts` exercises against `run-e2e.sh`'s one shared daemon.

Setting `STORYHOOK_WEB_TRUSTED_HOSTS` on the shared daemon to admit the fake hostname would therefore silently break coupon-arming for every other spec in the suite — discovered by reading the code path, not by running it broken.

## What's needed

A second `story daemon` instance, isolated from the shared one `run-e2e.sh` already starts:
- Its own `STORYHOOK_DATA_DIR`/store, so it never touches the shared daemon's state.
- `STORYHOOK_WEB_TRUSTED_HOSTS` set only in *its* environment, naming the fake hostname.
- Started and torn down around just the new spec(s) — not for the suite's whole run, so `behind_a_proxy()`'s effect stays scoped to the one daemon that needs it.
- A new Playwright project (matching the existing `chromium`/`mobile-chromium` split in `e2e/playwright.config.ts`) launched with the `--host-resolver-rules` flag and a `baseURL` pointing at the fake hostname on that second daemon's port.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A new e2e spec browses `http://storyhook.e2e.test:<port>` (a Chromium-resolver-mapped, non-potentially-trustworthy origin) and confirms: paste a valid named token, then reload / open a second tab / restart the daemon — no re-prompt at any step.
- [ ] The existing shared daemon and its specs (`handoff.spec.ts` in particular) are provably unaffected — call this out explicitly in the PR, and add a regression note near `local_request`'s doc comment or a test if a cheap one exists.
- [ ] `docs/spec/dashboard-authorization.md`'s SH-319 "As built" section is updated to point at this closed gap once done.
- [ ] `make test` (including `scripts/run-e2e.sh`) stays green.

## Out of scope
- Anything about the fix itself — SH-319 already shipped it, tested at the socket level, and verified manually. This story is purely about the missing automated browser leg.

payload.subject: docs(spec): record SH-319's fix and close SH-255's own merge gate

payload.title: Project-registration inputs are labelled by placeholder alone

payload.description:
## What

`buildInitForm()` (`src/web_dashboard.html:7886-7888`) labels its three project-registration inputs with a `placeholder` attribute and nothing else — no `<label>`, no `aria-label`.

## Why it matters

Three criteria, not one: SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships — the association between the prompt and the field exists only visually), SC 3.3.2 (Labels or Instructions), and SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value — the accessible name is unreliable; some AT reads a placeholder as the name, some does not, and none should be relied on to).

And the plain usability failure underneath all three: **the placeholder vanishes as soon as the user types**, so anyone who is interrupted mid-form has no way to recover what the field was for.

## Extent

Not surveyed. Found by the accessibility seat during SH-322's council while reading a neighbouring function; the sweep for other placeholder-as-label sites has not been done. `#create-title`, `#delete-reason` and `#drop-blocked-reason-input` all take placeholders and should be checked first — some may already have a visible heading that serves, some may not.

## Direction

Visible `<label for>` per input is the default answer and matches the file's own conventions elsewhere. Where the visual design genuinely cannot carry a visible label, `aria-label` is the fallback, not the first choice.

## Pin

Playwright can assert accessible names directly — `getByRole("textbox", { name: ... })` — so each field gets one assertion, and they fail today.

payload.title: post-git.sh's systemMessage branch is unreachable: --quiet empties the output it tests

payload.description:
## What

`plugin/claude-code/hooks/post-git.sh` ends with a branch that reports the sync back into the Claude Code transcript:

```sh
sync_output=$(story --deadline 8 commit-sync --since 1h --quiet 2>/dev/null || echo "")
if [[ -n "$sync_output" ]]; then
  ... print {"systemMessage": "[storyhook] Git sync: ..."}
```

`sync_output` is **always empty**, so that branch has never executed and the advertised `[storyhook] Git sync: …` line has never appeared in anyone's transcript.

The cause is the `--quiet` flag on the very call whose output is tested: `render_response` returns an empty string for any non-`RawJson` response when quiet is set (`src/output.rs:726`), and `commit-sync` returns `Response::Message` (`src/invoke.rs:754-755`).

## Extent

Cosmetic — nothing is lost but the notification. Worth recording that it cuts the other way for SH-330's cost argument: a redundant sync costs latency only, with zero transcript noise and zero tokens, which is *why* redundancy is genuinely cheap.

Either the flag or the branch is wrong, and that is the decision this story has to make:

- **Drop `--quiet`** and the message appears — but every merge, commit and pull then writes a line into the transcript, including the redundant syncs SH-330 deliberately added.
- **Drop the branch** and the hook always prints `{}` — honest, smaller, and admits the feature was never delivered.

Not obviously one or the other; decide before implementing.

## Where and how found

By the SH-330 council's challenger seat, while verifying the claim that a redundant sync is cheap. It is not a claim the brief made — the seat went looking for a cost and found the cost does not exist, for a reason nobody intended.

## Last known good

Unknown; plausibly never. The `--quiet` flag and the branch that tests its output appear to have been written together.

payload.title: POST_MERGE_HOOK's auto-close loop pays one deadline per trailer, so a persistently unreachable daemon can still cost N x 10s

payload.description:
## What

`POST_MERGE_HOOK`'s auto-close loop (`src/hooks.rs`) runs one `story move <id> done ...` per `Closes|Fixes|Resolves` trailer found in the merge's commit range, with no shared budget across iterations. After SH-343 gives that call `--deadline 10`, each individual call is bounded — but a merge whose commits carry N such trailers, against a daemon that stays unreachable throughout (not merely cold), still costs N x 10s total. A `git pull` bringing 20 trailers would still cost 200s.

## Why this is filed separately from SH-343, not folded in

Council verdict (unanimous 3-0), audit trail `.council/sh-343-scope-boundary/` in the SH-343 worktree:

1. **The obvious fix (a latch keyed on exit code 5) is unsafe as designed.** `src/error.rs:153` maps both `AppError::Integrity` and `AppError::Storage` to exit code 5, and `Storage` is constructed at over 160 call sites across the crate — it is not a clean "storyhook gave up" signal. A latch keyed on it would silently swallow genuine store errors as give-ups, inside a hook obliged to stay silent (`tests/hook_silence.rs`). A correct version needs a real give-up signal (distinct from an ordinary command failure), which does not exist today.
2. **SH-343's own trigger (a cold daemon) is already fully resolved** by `--deadline 10` on all four call sites: only the first `story` call in a hook pays a cold start, and every call after it hits a warm daemon. This story's residual needs the rarer, different fault of a daemon that stays unreachable for the whole hook's lifetime.
3. **Measured against this repo's own history:** the worst observed merge on `main` carries 5 trailers (359 of 454 merges carry zero), so the realistic worst case after SH-343 lands is ~60s — a large improvement over the pre-SH-343 ~750s (5 x 150s), even with this residual unfixed.

## What a fix here needs

- A real "storyhook gave up on this call" signal distinguishable from an ordinary per-story failure (already closed, no such story, etc.) — likely a new, narrower exit code or a stderr sentinel the hook can grep for even under `2>/dev/null` redirection tricks, or a `story` subcommand designed for batched give-up-aware execution.
- Its own regression tests proving it stops on a genuine give-up and does NOT stop on a benign per-story refusal (`tests/hook_execution.rs`).
- Care around the hook's silence contract (`tests/hook_silence.rs`) — the loop currently swallows every exit code via `|| true`; introducing a `$?` check is a behavioural shell change, not a flag insertion.

## Where and how found

By the SH-343 council, while deciding whether to fold this latch into that story's fix.

payload.subject: fix(hooks): every managed git hook gives up on storyhook before git gives up on it

payload.title: WebKit's default clipboard-write permission posture differs from Chromium's, breaking a deliberate-failure test fixture

payload.description:
## What

`e2e/specs/notice-autorepeat.spec.ts`'s `raiseDurableErrors()` helper deliberately does
NOT grant clipboard permission in this file's `beforeEach`, relying on
`navigator.clipboard.writeText()` failing so the dashboard's `copyText()` `.catch` branch
raises a durable ERROR notice instead of a success one (documented already in sibling
files, e.g. `notice-focus-indicator.spec.ts`'s own comment: "Without this the Copy-*
paths take copyText's .catch branch and raise an ERROR notice instead of a success").

Under Chromium this reliably works: an unpermitted write is denied, `copyText()` catches
the rejection, an error notice appears. Under WebKit (SH-335's new project) it does not:
`raiseDurableErrors()` asks for 3 error notices and gets 0, every time. The write appears
to succeed (or otherwise not throw) under WebKit even with no explicit `clipboard-write`
grant -- the opposite default posture from Chromium's automated/headless context.

This is a different finding from SH-335's own clipboard fix: that one was about
`grantPermissions(["clipboard-write"])` throwing outright under WebKit (no such
permission exists to grant there). This is about the UNGRANTED, default state: Chromium
defaults to denying an unpermitted write; WebKit does not.

## Consequence

5 of 6 tests in `notice-autorepeat.spec.ts` fail under `webkit`, all because their shared
setup (`raiseDurableErrors`) never produces the durable error notices the tests need --
not because of anything about held-key/`event.repeat` simulation, which is what the file
is actually about. `modal-enter-autorepeat.spec.ts`, which also exercises held-key
behavior via the same `holdKey()` helper but does not depend on a deliberately-failing
clipboard write, passes 12/12 clean under webkit -- confirming the auto-repeat mechanism
itself is fine cross-engine and this is purely the clipboard-default-posture gap.

## What to do

Find a cross-engine-reliable way to force `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` to fail on
demand -- e.g. an `addInitScript` that monkey-patches `navigator.clipboard.writeText` to
reject, rather than relying on ambient permission state, which apparently defaults
oppositely per engine. `story-context-menu.spec.ts:182`'s "copying still works when
navigator.clipboard doesn't exist" test already deletes `navigator.clipboard` entirely
via `addInitScript` for a related purpose and may be adaptable.

## Until it lands

The 5 affected tests are quarantined under `webkit` via `test.skip(browserName ===
"webkit", "... (SH-374)")`, fenced by `tests/e2e_browser_coverage.rs::
every_webkit_quarantine_names_a_story`. Fully load-bearing under `chromium`.

Filed during SH-335 (adding a `webkit` Playwright project) after a post-rebase
verification run surfaced this file, which landed on `main` after SH-335's branch point
(SH-339) and was never triaged against WebKit until now.

payload.title: A card re-claimed after being unclaimed can still be silently removed 600ms later

payload.description:
Sibling defect found during SH-397's investigation, deliberately not folded into that fix (`story show SH-397`).

`removeUnclaimedCards()` (`src/web_dashboard.html`) marks any board card node not claimed by the current render `.exiting`, and defers its real `node.remove()` behind either an `animationend` listener or a 600ms `setTimeout` safety net (`5991-5996` at the time of filing), whichever fires first.

`populateCard()` re-claims a card by doing `card.className = "card" + (...)` (`6261` at time of filing) -- a full overwrite, which silently wipes the `.exiting` class (and `.entering`/`.moving`/`.flash-*`) if the SAME story reappears in a later render after being unclaimed in an earlier one (e.g. filtered out then back in; column visibility toggled; a rapid pair of renders where the story's slug flaps). The card becomes a normal, live, clickable card again -- but the `setTimeout` armed against it when it was unclaimed is never cancelled, and since `.exiting` is gone, `animationend` will never fire for it either (nothing is animating). 600ms after the ORIGINAL unclaim, the safety-net timer fires anyway and calls `node.remove()` on a node that is, by then, live and wanted -- silently deleting a visible card out from under the user with no error and no warning.

Not the cause of SH-397's two reported occurrences (both are fresh-open sequences, not unclaim-then-reclaim sequences), so it earns its own story per this project's sibling-sweep rule rather than being folded into that fix.

Fix shape (not yet designed): the `setTimeout` needs to be cancelled, or made to no-op, if the card is re-claimed before it fires -- most likely by keying it to the SAME per-card token/generation scheme `.exiting`'s own animation-vs-timeout race already needs, checked against the card node's *current* class list (or an explicit re-claim counter) at fire time rather than assuming the class it saw when armed still applies 600ms later. Needs a reproduction spec forcing the unclaim/reclaim/timer-fire sequence deterministically (a `holdFetch`-gated pair of `/data` replies, one that omits the story and one that restores it inside the 600ms window) before any fix, per this project's reproduce-before-fix doctrine.

payload.subject: fix(dashboard): make a card's presentational body immune to a mid-click re-render

payload.title: The dashboard's ~16 bare DOM-removal sites should funnel through one detach() door

payload.description:
Severed from SH-401 by unanimous council motion, including the winning proposal own author, who named it "the weakest part" of that proposal and "severable without touching the behaviour of the fix"; the other two seats each named it as the one thing they held against the winner. See story show SH-401 for the full verdict (SH-363: cite the story, never the council directory, which does not survive worktree teardown).

WHAT. src/web_dashboard.html destroys DOM through several idioms: clear() (the one named door, ~37 call sites), bare node.remove(), removeChild(), and assignment forms. SH-401 press gate is fenced by a MutationObserver, which is COMPLETE over removal MECHANISMS (blind to no idiom, including one written next year) and INCOMPLETE over SURFACES (it observes only what a spec run actually exercises). A static scan is the exact mirror: complete over the surfaces it can name, blind to any idiom it was not taught. Both halves are wanted; only the observer half ships with SH-401.

This story is the static half. Funnel every removal through a single detach() beside clear(), then fence it with a Rust scan derived over IDIOMS rather than sites — .remove(), removeChild(, replaceChildren(, innerHTML = outside that one pair — with a positive control so a parser that stopped recognising the file fails instead of reporting a clean tree. That is the shape tests/dead_public_surface.rs and tests/store_isolation.rs already use, and the reason it matters here is recorded twice in SH-401 own council: one seat proposed a static clear()-shaped scan, was shown blind to ten bare .remove() sites, and WITHDREW it mid-council rather than ship a fence with that hole.

WHY SEPARATE. It is a pure refactor across ~16 call sites with zero behaviour change, so two hats puts it in its own commit regardless; folding it into a behaviour fix would make the fix unbisectable. It is also not a prerequisite: the press gate is correct without it, and the observer already catches the class at runtime.

DONE WHEN. Every removal in src/web_dashboard.html goes through clear() or detach(); a derived Rust test fails on a new bare removal added anywhere in the file, mutation-verified in both directions; make test green.

payload.title: populateCard's className overwrite wipes transient animation/drag classes

payload.description:
Sibling defect found during SH-399's investigation, filed separately -- different hat (cosmetic, not a click-swallowing race), cheap fix, no reason to ride along on SH-399's behavior-fixing commit.

`populateCard()` (src/web_dashboard.html:6757) writes `card.className = "card" + (state.pending[st.id] ? " pending" : "") + (draggable ? "" : " not-draggable")` -- a wholesale overwrite of the element's class list on every render. This silently wipes any transient state class that happens to be live at that moment: `.dragging` (added by `buildCard`'s own `dragstart` listener, :6733), `.entering`/`.moving` (added by `reconcileColumnCards`/`playFlip`'s FLIP animation), and any `flash-*` class (`applyChangeFlash`). A render landing mid-drag drops the drag-affordance opacity/rotation; a render landing mid-FLIP-animation can cut a slide short; a render landing mid-flash cancels the pulse.

Fix: use `classList.add`/`classList.remove`/`classList.toggle` for the two DERIVED classes (`pending`, `not-draggable`) instead of a wholesale `className =` overwrite, so any transient class added by another code path survives. Cheap, isolated, no architectural risk -- suggested priority low (friction/inconsistency, not truth -- per this project's priority rubric, nothing false is stored and nothing is silently lost, just a visual glitch that self-corrects on the next render).

payload.subject: fix(dashboard): defer the paint while a press is in flight

payload.title: Per-store launchd labels let stray login agents accumulate with only enumeration, no bound or cleanup

payload.description:
What. SH-414 gave the default store's login agent (bare label) and every other store's (label plus key) each their own launchd label, which removed a side effect that used to bound accumulation: before SH-414 a second `story daemon install` for a different store always collided with and replaced whatever was at the one shared label, so at most one stray agent could ever exist. Per-store labels coexist instead, so an operator can now accumulate N login agents, including one for a store under a temp directory that no longer exists, each still re-launching a defunct daemon at every login (no `KeepAlive`, so it does not respawn, but it does still fire once per login forever until manually uninstalled).

Where. src/daemon/agent.rs (label, install), src/daemon/install_guard.rs (the install gate).

How found. Weighed and explicitly not adopted during SH-414's design: refusing an install for a store under a temp directory was considered and measured against this suite -- `is_under_temp` (src/service/project.rs) counts `/private/tmp`, and `Environment::at(tempdir_in("/private/tmp"))` is how every daemon-install test fixture builds its own *default* store, so a temp-store refusal placed ahead of every side effect (where any such gate must go) would refuse the suite's own default-store installs. This project has also already tried and reverted the sibling substitution once for a different guard (`is_default()` in place of `is_under_temp` for `refuse_temp_project_in_real_store`, docs/spec/store-isolation.md's As-built item 7), for the identical fake-HOME reason -- so this is a genuinely harder design question than SH-414's own scope, not a one-line fix.

Extent. Symptomless friction, not data loss: SH-414 shipped `agent::report`/`describe_others`, so every other login agent on the machine is already named by `story daemon status`, `install`, and `uninstall` -- an operator who runs any of those sees the accumulation and can `story --store-path <the stray store> daemon uninstall` it by hand. Nothing false is stored; this is purely about whether the tool should also bound or auto-clean the accumulation rather than only report it.

Fix direction, not prescriptive. A predicate distinguishing "a store worth a permanent login agent" from "a throwaway one" needs its own design (this story's litigation already ruled out both `is_under_temp` and `is_default()` on their own); or a reaper that removes an agent whose store file no longer exists, run opportunistically from `status`/`install`; or simply leaving enumeration as the whole answer and closing this without a code change, if a council judges visibility sufficient.

Priority reasoning. Low: friction, not truth -- costs time and disk-adjacent tidiness, has an obvious workaround (the enumeration SH-414 already shipped, then a manual uninstall), and nothing currently filed depends on this tooling existing.

payload.title: launchctl bootout's result is discarded on both install and uninstall, hiding a real refusal behind the expected 'nothing was loaded' case

payload.description:
What. Every `launchctl bootout` invocation on the login-agent surface discards its result: `bootstrap_via_launchctl`'s bootout call (src/daemon/commands.rs) and `bootout_via_launchctl` (the same file, `uninstall`'s unload closure) both use `let _ = Command::new("launchctl")...output();`. `bootout` legitimately fails when nothing was loaded under that label, which is the common and expected case on a fresh install -- so today's blanket discard is defensible for that one case. But it also silently swallows a REAL refusal (a permissions problem, a malformed domain target, or any other reason launchctl declines) indistinguishably from "nothing was loaded," and it silently swallows the io::Error case of `launchctl` itself being missing or unspawnable.

Where. src/daemon/commands.rs (bootstrap_via_launchctl, bootout_via_launchctl).

How found. Named as a pre-existing gap during SH-414's design (the launchd-label fix), on both the install and uninstall paths -- unrelated to labels specifically, since it was present before SH-414 too, but surfaced while reworking both functions to be store-scoped.

Extent. Symptomless: an operator running `story daemon install` or `uninstall` gets a success message even when the underlying `bootout` half genuinely failed for a reason other than "nothing was loaded" -- the visible symptom, if any, only shows up later as a stale or duplicate-seeming agent, with no diagnostic pointing back to the swallowed launchctl failure.

Fix direction, not prescriptive. Distinguish "no such service" (exit 113, or whatever this machine's launchctl reports for "nothing was loaded") from every other nonzero exit, and surface the latter as a warning rather than silence -- on both the install path (ahead of the bootstrap that follows) and the uninstall path (in the returned message, the way SH-414 already made uninstall report a foreign-store agent).

Priority reasoning. Low: symptomless debt outside the detection layer (this is an operational diagnostic gap in `story daemon install/uninstall` themselves, not in the test suite's own ability to catch a filed defect), with an obvious workaround -- running `launchctl print`/`bootout` by hand to see what actually happened.

payload.title: default_daemon_port uses is_default() instead of the login-time-default predicate, the same gap SH-414 fixed for the launchd label

payload.description:
What. `Environment::from_process` picks the daemon's preferred port with `default_daemon_port(store.is_default())` (src/env/mod.rs) -- the identical `is_default()` predicate SH-414 found and replaced for the launchd label, on a different surface. `store.is_default()` answers relative to whatever `$XDG_DATA_HOME` the current process has, not what a launchd-started (environment-stripped) daemon for the true login-time default would resolve. So a store reached only via `$XDG_DATA_HOME` -- e.g. `XDG_DATA_HOME=/scratch story daemon start` -- reads as `is_default() == true` and requests the stable `DEFAULT_DAEMON_PORT` (3456), the same port the machine's real default-store daemon (started by its login agent, or by any other client) also prefers.

Where. src/env/mod.rs (default_daemon_port, Environment::from_process).

How found. Named while fixing SH-414's own label predicate, as a sibling instance of the identical `is_default()`-vs-login-time-default gap on a different surface (the port, not the label).

Extent. Self-healing, not silent-wrong-answer: `serve::bind_listeners`/`bind_preferred` (per docs/spec/store-isolation.md's Ports section and SH-253) already falls back from a preferred-but-unavailable port to an OS-assigned one on a bind collision, and daemon identity is keyed off the store path (SH-113's `daemon_state_dir`), never off the port -- so a client resolving which daemon serves which store is unaffected by which port either daemon happens to bind. The only visible symptom is a scratch store's daemon occasionally landing on the "wrong" (non-3456) port through no fault other than a collision it already recovers from, which is confusing at most, never a stored falsehood or a client talking to the wrong store.

Fix direction, not prescriptive. The same predicate SH-414 introduced for the label, `daemon::agent::serves_the_login_default` (or the same reasoning inlined here), in place of `store.is_default()` for this one call site -- likely the smallest fix in this whole family of residuals, since the predicate already exists.

Priority reasoning. Low: self-healing by an existing fallback, confirmed no stored falsehood and no wrong-store routing, so this is friction/confusion at most rather than anything the priority rubric's damage ladder ranks above that.

payload.subject: fix(dashboard): make a card's own rebuild conditional, closing .rel-id's mid-click race

payload.title: orphan_check::postlude_fails_when_a_survivor_outlives_sigkill flakes under full-suite load

payload.description:
## What

`tests/orphan_check.rs::postlude_fails_when_a_survivor_outlives_sigkill` fails intermittently under full-suite parallel load. Observed 2026-08-25 during a `make test` on a docs-only branch, load average 4.75-6.72 on a 10-core M1 Max:

    thread 'postlude_fails_when_a_survivor_outlives_sigkill' panicked at tests/orphan_check.rs:462:5:
    a survivor of SIGKILL must fail the postlude rather than certify a tree over a real leak
    stderr:
    test result: FAILED. 6 passed; 1 failed

Note `stderr:` is EMPTY -- the postlude said nothing at all, it simply succeeded.

## Reproduction status

Does NOT reproduce in isolation: 3/3 passes running that test alone at load 6.72, ~15.9s each. It needs the other test binaries competing. That is the signature this project already carries several stories for (SH-221, SH-349, SH-375, SH-378, SH-395) -- load-sensitive, full-suite-only.

## The mechanism, and the question that decides how bad this is

The fixture spawns a supervisor that respawns a daemon every 0.05s for 18 seconds, so that a survivor always exists no matter how many times the postlude kills one. The test sleeps 600ms, runs `postlude`, and asserts it FAILS.

It passed instead, which means the postlude's final verification found no process. Two possible causes, and they carry very different weight:

1. **THE FIXTURE WAS STARVED.** Under heavy load the supervisor's respawn loop did not get scheduled during the postlude's verification window, so there genuinely was no survivor to find. The gate was right; the fixture lied to it -- SH-263's exact shape, one layer over.
2. **THE POSTLUDE HAS A REAL WINDOW** in which it can certify a tree while a leaked daemon exists. That is a defect in the detection layer itself: `scripts/check-no-orphan-servers.sh`'s postlude is what certifies that a run left nothing behind (SH-412), and a postlude that can miss a survivor certifies over a real leak.

Cause 1 is far more likely given it never reproduces in isolation. But nothing has established that, and the difference matters: cause 2 would mean the orphan bracket can pass over exactly the condition it exists to catch.

## Priority reasoning

Filed `low` per the rubric's explicit rule that individual flakes stay low -- each costs one re-run, and the gate still catches real reds. RE-PRICE IT if investigation shows cause 2: a defect in the postlude itself falls under the detection-layer carve-out and caps at `high`, because the orphan bracket is the only coverage that observes this leak class.

## Fix shape

Establish which cause first -- do not fix before that is known. Instrument the fixture to record whether a supervisor-spawned process actually existed at the moment the postlude ran; if it did and the postlude still passed, that is cause 2 and a different story. If it did not, the fixture needs a starvation-proof way to guarantee a survivor during the verification window -- and per this project's own rule, any wall-clock in the fix derives from the deadline it is proving rather than being a bare literal (SH-394). The 600ms sleep and the 18s supervisor deadline are both bare literals today.

## Context

Found while landing docs for the Full Auto engine. Not caused by that change -- the branch touched only `docs/spec/full-auto-engine.md`, and the `fmt`, `clippy` and `rust-suite` legs were all REUSED, so only `rust-contracts` ran.

payload.title: Separate project roadmap from generated AGENTS template

payload.description:
## Problem

The repository-specific Mini-roadmap is duplicated in root AGENTS.md and the reusable templates::agents_md output, while tests/scope_rubric.rs requires whole-file byte equality. Intentional roadmap edits therefore require synchronized product-template edits and have repeatedly produced follow-up repairs (7ce3a293, cf1e775d, 106a887e, and SH-552/PR #634). The contract catches drift loudly, so no false state ships, but normal roadmap maintenance repeatedly blocks unrelated pull requests.

## Direction

Separate immutable generated StoryHook instructions from project-owned roadmap content, preferably using the existing BEGIN/END STORYHOOK ownership boundary. Keep the local roadmap outside the generated block and compare only the generated block to templates::agents_md. Ensure scaffold output contains no StoryHook-repository story IDs or roadmap.

## Acceptance criteria

- Updating root AGENTS.md roadmap requires one edit.
- Generated StoryHook instructions remain exactly fenced against drift.
- story scaffold agents-md emits no repository-specific roadmap or SH story ID.
- Setup refreshes the generated block while preserving local roadmap bytes.
- Tests reject missing, duplicate, or reversed ownership sentinels.

## Origin

Discovered during light RCA for SH-552 after centralized verification caught scope_rubric::this_repos_agents_md_is_what_the_template_generates. This is separate architectural work and must not be mixed into PR #634.

payload.title: Full Auto start opens a config dialog; the run carries agent, lanes, model, effort and speed

payload.description:
Part 1 of SH-565. ## Context Starting a Full Auto run today configures almost nothing. `engine_runs` (`src/store/schema/0024_engine_runs.sql`) carries `agent` and `lanes` and no model, effort or speed column. `src/service/engine.rs`'s `DispatchOptions` doc (around line 366) states the position directly: *"An engine (Full Auto) lane always passes this default: SH-517 does not extend model/effort/speed selection to engine lanes"* — `DispatchRequest` has only `project`, `story`, `agent`, and `run_shell_dispatch` therefore appends none of `--model`/`--effort`/`--speed` to the helper argv. The dashboard is narrower still. `buildEngineLaunchControl` renders an inline lane-count number input and a Run button; `startEngineRun` posts `{lanes: n}` or `{epic: id}` and nothing else, so every dashboard-started run takes the `claude` default with no way to choose Codex, a model, an effort or fast mode. The epic drawer's own "Run Full Auto on this epic" control (near line 10416) posts `{epic}` alone for the same reason. The attended path already has all of this. SH-517 built the `dispatch-modal` (agent, model, effort, speed) backed by `GET /api/dispatch-options`, with a per-provider catalog, remembered selections and `populateDispatchSelector`. This story gives Full Auto the same questions. ## What is needed Server: - A migration adding nullable `model`, `effort` and `speed` (or a `fast` flag) to `engine_runs`. No schema CHECK on model/effort: those vocabularies come from a provider catalog that changes under us, so a CHECK would refuse a model the provider added. `speed`/`fast` IS a closed vocabulary and should carry one, per 0024's own "every finite vocabulary written here is guarded by a schema CHECK" rule. - `StartRequest` carries the selections; they are persisted on the run and returned on `RunView` so the dashboard can show what a live run was started with. - `DispatchRequest` carries them per lane, and `run_shell_dispatch` builds the `--model`/`--effort`/`--speed` argv it already knows how to build. Replace the `DispatchOptions` doc paragraph quoted above; do not leave it asserting the opposite of what the code now does. - `POST /api/repos/

/engine` accepts them, validated at the HTTP boundary by the same charset-gated `OptionToken` `crate::api::dispatch` already uses — these strings reach a shell argv. - `story engine start` gains `--model `, `--effort `, `--speed standard|fast`, and `story help engine` documents them. Every complete parse arm still ends in `expect_no_more` (SH-357). Dashboard: - The inline lane input and the Run button collapse into a single "Run Full Auto" button that opens a config modal asking **agent, lanes, model, effort and speed** — user determination, 2026-09-05. - The modal reuses SH-517's catalog: `GET /api/dispatch-options`, the same per-provider filtering, and the same remembered-selection behaviour. - The epic drawer's "Run Full Auto on this epic" control opens the same modal, scoped to that epic. - Mutating submit carries an in-flight guard, and an ambiguous transport outcome (`status: 0`) is reported as ambiguous, never as failure (SH-312). ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A run started from the dashboard with a non-default agent/model/effort/speed dispatches its lanes with exactly those flags on the `story.sh dispatch` argv, proven by a test that reads the built argv rather than the UI. - [ ] The same selections round-trip through `story engine start` and appear on `story engine status --json`. - [ ] A run started with no selections produces argv byte-identical to today's. - [ ] The migration is proven by the existing migration harness, and a fixture seeding this table derives its vocabulary from the writer (SH-364). - [ ] An e2e spec opens the modal, chooses a non-default value, starts a run and asserts the request body. Runs on both engine pairs (SH-335). - [ ] `docs/spec/full-auto-engine.md` records the change in its "As built" section, including that D-series decisions did not previously cover per-run provider options. ## Out of scope - Changing a live run's options. A run is configured at start. - Per-lane heterogeneous options within one run. - Pause/Stop controls (sibling story), the acknowledgement modal (sibling story), and the lane chip (sibling story).

payload.text:
# SH-566 — Configurable Full Auto Runs

## Summary

Add immutable provider configuration to Full Auto runs. Project and epic launch buttons open one dedicated configuration modal. The selected agent, lane count, model, effort, and speed persist with the run, appear in status responses, and propagate unchanged to every lane dispatch.

```text
Dashboard / CLI / HTTP
        │
        ▼
StartRequest { scope, lanes, agent, model, effort, speed }
        │
        ▼
EngineRunRecord ── migration 31 ── engine_runs
        │
        ├──► CLI/HTTP/dashboard RunView
        │
        ▼
DispatchRequest per lane
        │
        ▼
ShellDispatcher ──► story.sh dispatch ... [--model] [--effort] [--speed]
```

## Implementation

1. Before changing files or running tests, run `story comment SH-566 "<approved plan>"`, using the exact Markdown between the `<proposed_plan>` tags in this response, verbatim. Record every later implementation decision on SH-566 before continuing, as required by the autonomous-session charter.
2. Write failing tests first, then add migration 31 with nullable `model`, `effort`, and `speed` columns. Constrain speed to `standard|fast`; leave model and effort unconstrained by catalog membership. Existing rows migrate to `NULL`. Add a documented `EngineSpeed` enum and extend `EngineRunRecord`, SQLite hydration, and creation writes; run updates keep configuration immutable.
3. Extend `EngineAction::Start`, `StartRequest`, and `DispatchRequest` with model, effort, and optional speed. Factor the existing `OptionToken` character/length rule into one shared validator used by attended dispatch, CLI parsing, HTTP deserialization, and the service boundary. Reject forged wire values before storage.
4. Add CLI flags `--model <id>`, `--effort <id>`, and `--speed standard|fast`, retaining `expect_no_more`. Extend CLI and HTTP run views with nullable `model`, `effort`, and `speed`; human status renders absent values as `default`. Explicit `standard` round-trips but emits no helper flag, matching attended dispatch; `fast` emits `--speed=fast`. Omitted options preserve the current helper argv byte-for-byte.
5. Replace the inline lane input and launch button with one “Run Full Auto” button. Add a dedicated Full Auto modal containing Provider, Lanes, Model, Effort, and Speed. Both project and epic actions open it; epic submissions include the epic ID and selected lane count.
6. Reuse the existing dispatch-options fetch/cache and provider-filtered selector logic. Share remembered agent/model/effort/speed preferences with attended dispatch, but do not change its Auto-mode preference from a Full Auto submission. Save only on submit; Cancel discards edits and restores focus.
7. Guard submission synchronously with the existing per-project in-flight claim. Disable duplicate activation, preserve the “Starting Full Auto…” state, and retain the follow-up status fetch. A status-0 transport result remains explicitly ambiguous and never claims failure.
8. Show the live run’s provider and explicit/default model, effort, and speed beside its existing state and lane count. Include configuration in the render fingerprint so server refreshes cannot leave stale metadata.
9. Update `story help engine`, top-level CLI usage, README examples, and `docs/spec/full-auto-engine.md`. Add an SH-566 “As built” entry explaining that the original D-series omitted per-run provider options. Refresh the AGENTS.md mini-roadmap and replace HANDOFF.md with the submission and verification state.

## Tests

- Migration/store tests: v30→v31 preserves existing runs with null options; allowed speed values come from `EngineSpeed::as_str`; invalid speed and corrupt stored tokens fail loudly; configured records survive reopen and status reads.
- Service/dispatcher tests: reconciliation copies persisted options into every `DispatchRequest`; selected options produce the exact helper argv; an unconfigured run retains the exact pre-SH-566 argv.
- CLI/wire tests: new flags parse in any supported order, invalid or trailing values refuse, all values survive daemon invocation, and `engine start/status --json` round-trip them.
- HTTP tests: accepted fields return in run views; unsafe model/effort tokens, unknown speed values, and unknown JSON fields return 400-class responses.
- Dashboard tests: the old lane input is absent; project and epic buttons open the same modal; provider changes rebuild the catalog; Cancel does not save; submit sends `{epic?, lanes, agent, model?, effort?, speed?}`; duplicate submission and ambiguous transport behavior remain guarded.
- Run focused Rust targets for engine storage, reconciliation, dispatcher, CLI grammar, wire envelopes, HTTP/web endpoints, help, and snapshots. Run `scripts/run-e2e.sh specs/engine.spec.ts` across all four configured Chromium/WebKit desktop/mobile projects. Run formatting and warnings-as-errors checks. Do not run `make test` or any release/version command.

## Submission

- Keep commits focused and Conventional Commit formatted: backend persistence/API/CLI, dashboard behavior/E2E, then documentation and handoff. Run each commit’s directly impacted tests before creating it.
- Push `worktree-SH-566` over HTTPS. Open exactly one PR whose title contains `SH-566` and whose body references Storyhook story SH-566.
- Run `story link-pr SH-566 <PR-URL>`, then comment the same PR URL on SH-566.
- If an unrecoverable stop occurs, first comment full diagnostics, run `story block SH-566 "<reason>"`, preserve the worktree, and stop.
- Make `story move SH-566 verifying` the absolute final action. Do not merge, complete, reap, version, or deploy from this worktree.

## Assumptions

- Defaults remain lanes `1`, agent `claude`, and no model/effort/speed override.
- Run configuration cannot change after creation and is homogeneous across its lanes.
- `/story do <epic> --auto` and sibling SH-567–SH-569 controls remain out of scope.
- The centralized verifier owns the full suite, merge, completion, and cleanup.

## MIKEY ACTIONS

1. Approve this plan once. No later input is required.

Implementation decision — bounded migration fixtures: migration_28 must remain stopped at schema 28 and assert recent_quarantines_json through raw SQLite. The current EngineRunRecord reader now correctly targets schema 31 and therefore cannot read a deliberately older schema without columns model/effort/speed. I weighed sweeping migration 31 into the old test versus raw inspection; sweeping would stop proving migration 28 in isolation and contradict this repo's bounded-migration convention. Raw SQL preserves the test's exact subject.

payload.title: Nothing detects a commit made under the wrong author identity

payload.description:
## What

Nothing in this repository detects a commit made under the wrong author
identity. On 2026-09-05, five commits were authored and committed as
`t <t@t>` — the test-fixture identity — and every one of them was written,
pushed, gated, reviewed and merged without a single surface saying anything.
They are on `main` permanently:

    668ae0a0f 21:17:30Z fix(verification): isolate speculative git administration (SH-563)
    a01af0b2b 21:37:44Z fix(plugin): bind managed Claude launches
    46858590a 21:46:07Z docs(rca): record Claude dispatch dependency
    58cc74ac9 21:47:06Z feat(dashboard): add Full Auto lifecycle controls
    f94d1c671 21:47:14Z docs: update SH-567 handoff and roadmap

SH-572 closed the **cause** those five had: a fixture wrote `user.name t` /
`user.email t@t` into the shared `.git/config` under a leaked `GIT_DIR`. This
story is about the **detector**, which does not exist and which SH-572 did not
add. Identity can go wrong for reasons SH-572 cannot reach: a fresh clone with
no identity configured, an agent invoking `git -c user.email=…`, a
`GIT_AUTHOR_*` / `GIT_COMMITTER_*` pair inherited from a parent process, a
future config writer nobody has thought of. Every one of those produces the
same permanent, silent, unrepairable-after-push result.

## Why this is worth a detector rather than a note

A commit object is the one artifact in this system that is genuinely
**append-only and unrepairable in place**. Everything else this project guards
— the store, the read model, the receipt, the config — can be rebuilt, doctored
or re-derived. Authorship, once pushed and merged, can only be corrected by
rewriting published history, which this project forbids on `main`. So the
window in which a wrong identity is fixable is the few seconds between `git
commit` and `git push`, and today nothing looks at it in that window or ever
after.

It is also the exact damage-ladder rung 1 case the priority rubric describes:
the system stores a false statement, on a supported path, and does not say so
at the time. It sat undetected through five commits, four pull requests, a
release gate and a merge.

## Where the gap is

- `.githooks/` carries `post-commit`, `post-merge`, `prepare-commit-msg` and
  `pre-push`. None reads author identity. There is no `pre-commit` chainer at
  all.
- `.githooks/pre-push` is the natural last line — it already inspects the
  pushed range — but it currently only asks about gate receipts.
- `story doctor` audits the store, never the repository's commit metadata.
- `scripts/merge-preflight.sh` computes the exact merge tree and never looks at
  who authored the parents.

## Design constraints — the hard part, recorded rather than decided

The obvious implementation is wrong twice over, and both traps are ones this
project has already paid for:

1. **No bare literal.** A hook that refuses anything other than
   `mw@mikey.io` is a personal identity compiled into a tool other people
   install. The check has to *derive* the expected identity, exactly as
   `SH-394` requires a ceiling to derive from the deadline it disproves and
   `SH-406` derives build identity from the tracked tree rather than a version
   string.
2. **No denylist of fixture identities.** Refusing `t@t` and
   `e2e@storyhook.test` is the shape SH-160's council explicitly voted down —
   two of three seats voted against their own denylist proposals once four
   missing names were found during the vote. A new fixture identity would walk
   straight past it.

One candidate that satisfies both, offered as a starting point and not as the
answer: refuse when `user.email` is set at **repository-local** scope and
disagrees with the **global** value. That is derived from the machine's own
configuration, needs no allowlist, needs no literal, is silent for everyone
whose repo-local identity is deliberate and matching, and would have caught all
five of these — the fixture wrote repo-local while global stayed correct. Its
weakness is equally clear and should be weighed: a developer who legitimately
sets a per-repository identity (a work address on a personal machine) is
exactly the case it would refuse, so it likely needs an opt-in escape that is
itself recorded rather than silent.

Whether the check belongs at `pre-commit` (cheapest to correct, but git ignores
a `pre-commit` failure's status? — no: git obeys it, unlike `post-commit`; see
SH-355 for which hook statuses git actually honours) or at `pre-push` (catches
a commit made with hooks bypassed, but only after the fact) or both is a real
decision. So is whether `story doctor` should sweep existing history. This
should be settled by council rather than by whoever picks the story up.

## Extent

The sweep half matters as much as the gate half: nothing today can answer "has
this ever happened before?" without a hand-written `git log --format` filter.
A repository-wide audit is a few seconds of work and belongs in `story doctor`
or a script, so the question is askable rather than reconstructed each time.

## Reproduction

    git config user.email t@t && git config user.name t
    git commit --allow-empty -m 'proof'
    git log -1 --format='%an <%ae>'      # => t <t@t>, no warning anywhere
    git push                             # accepted, no warning anywhere

## Last known good

Never. No release of this repository has ever checked commit authorship.

## Regression test

Real git, in the `tests/push_gate.rs` and `tests/hooks.rs` style: a fixture
repository with a mismatched repo-local identity must be refused (or reported,
per whatever the council settles), and one with a matching or absent
repo-local identity must pass untouched. Mutation-check in both directions —
disable the check and confirm the refusal test goes red; widen it and confirm
the clean-identity test goes red.

## Relationship to SH-572

`relates-to`, never `blocked-by`. SH-572 removed one cause; this removes the
blindness. Neither depends on the other.

payload.title: The pinned release toolchain is assembled into a directory named after the host target triple, which defeats rustc sysroot autodetection

payload.description:
WHAT: `scripts/release.sh --bump <level>` cannot get past its own preflight. `scripts/build-release-assets.sh --check` dies on the Darwin capability probe with rustc E0463 "can't find crate for `std`; the aarch64-apple-darwin target may not be installed; consider `rustup target add aarch64-apple-darwin`" — a diagnosis that is wrong in both halves: the target IS installed, and rustup is not involved anywhere in this path.

WHERE: `scripts/release-toolchain.sh`, `ensure_release_toolchain`. It assembles the pinned toolchain at `$cache_root/toolchains/$lock_hash/$host_target`, so the sysroot`'s own final path component is literally `aarch64-apple-darwin`. rustc auto-detects its sysroot from the location of the librustc_driver dylib it loaded, and a dylib sitting at `<X>/<target-triple>/lib/` is read as the `$sysroot/lib/rustlib/$target/lib` layout — so it pops four components instead of one and reports `$cache_root` as the sysroot. `target-libdir` then resolves under `target/release-support/lib/rustlib/...`, which holds nothing, and every compile fails for want of std.

WHEN / LAST KNOWN GOOD: introduced by 0da1b66a0 "fix(release): build artifacts from pinned local capabilities", which is after the v2.4.0 tag. The pinned-toolchain path has therefore never assembled a release. v2.4.0 (2026-09-04) is the last version cut, and it predates this code.

EXTENT: every release target, not just the probe. The Darwin builds call `$toolchain/bin/cargo build --target ...` against the same toolchain, and `scripts/release-linux.sh` sources the same `ensure_release_toolchain` and reproduces the identical layout inside the Lima guest. All four archives are blocked.

REPRO (deterministic, toggles on the directory name alone):
  1. bash scripts/build-release-assets.sh --check   # E0463
  2. tc=target/release-support/toolchains/<lock_hash>/aarch64-apple-darwin
     "$tc/bin/rustc" --print sysroot                # prints target/release-support, not $tc
     "$tc/bin/rustc" --sysroot "$tc" --target aarch64-apple-darwin -C linker=clang probe.rs   # succeeds
  3. cp -R "$tc" /tmp/x/tc  && /tmp/x/tc/bin/rustc --print sysroot   # correct
     mv /tmp/x/tc /tmp/x/a/b/aarch64-apple-darwin
     /tmp/x/a/b/aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustc --print sysroot       # wrong again
  The toolchain contents are byte-identical across 3; only the leaf directory name changes.

FIX SHAPE: the assembled sysroot must not be named like a target triple, and the assembly must verify its own auto-detected sysroot rather than assuming it — a loud named refusal in place of rustc E0463 pointing at rustup.

payload.title: The desktop-Chromium browser project is red on origin/main: four failures, three of them one assertion, and the release tier is unobtainable

payload.description:
## What

A full desktop-Chromium browser run against clean `origin/main` (`cea6ec6d1`)
is **red**: 403 passed, **4 failed**, 11.7 minutes. No open story covers any of
them, and all five previously filed stories in this family are closed
(SH-401, SH-419, SH-349, SH-375, SH-378).

`make browser-status` reports **`never`** — no tree in `origin/main`'s
794-commit first-parent history has ever passed the browser suite. Because
`scripts/release.sh` requires `make test-full` and refuses `--skip-gate`
outside `--local-only`, this is not merely untidy: **no release can currently
be cut.**

## The four failures

| # | spec | assertion |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `description-edit-mode.spec.ts:279` — clicking the Comments toggle straight from edit mode both saves and toggles the section | `.section-toggle` `aria-expanded` expected `false`, got `true` |
| 2 | `dispatch.spec.ts:121` — Dispatch opens with defaults and does not remember cancelled edits | `#dispatch-model option` `toHaveText` failed; locator resolved to 5 elements |
| 3 | `drawer-body-click-race.spec.ts:134` — a /data reply landing between mousedown and mouseup does not swallow a drawer section toggle's click (SH-401) | `aria-expanded` expected `false`, got `true` |
| 4 | `drawer-body-click-race.spec.ts:179` — the same down/up choreography toggles the section when nothing re-renders in between | `aria-expanded` expected `false`, got `true` |

Every one timed out at 5000ms after the locator resolved 14 times, so these are
"the state never changed", not "the element was never found".

## The observation that matters most

Three of the four are the **same** assertion on the **same** control: the
Comments `.section-toggle` stayed `aria-expanded="true"` after a click that
should have collapsed it.

Case 4 is the load-bearing one. It is case 3's **control** — *"when nothing
re-renders in between"*. SH-401's press gate exists for the case where a
re-render destroys the click target before `mouseup`, so a click that fails
with **nothing re-rendering** is outside the mechanism SH-401 describes. Either
the control is no longer controlling what it thinks it is, or the toggle has a
defect that has nothing to do with the press gate.

That is why this is filed as one story rather than three: the shared assertion
and the failing control point at one cause, and splitting them first would
triage the same defect three times.

## Where

- `src/web_dashboard.html` — the section-toggle handler and the SH-401 press
  gate (`docs/spec/render-under-a-press.md`).
- `e2e/specs/description-edit-mode.spec.ts`, `drawer-body-click-race.spec.ts`,
  `dispatch.spec.ts`.

## Reproduction

    bash scripts/run-e2e.sh --project=chromium

Measured once, 2026-09-06, on `origin/main` `cea6ec6d1`, machine load average
2.90 on 10 cores at start. **Reproduce before fixing**, and record the load
average with each attempt: SH-347 makes load a first-class variable in this
suite, and its own doctrine is that a budget bends to contention while a base
budget does not. A 5000ms `expect` that fails after 14 resolutions is not
obviously a contention failure — the state genuinely never changed — but that
must be measured rather than assumed, because the five closed siblings were all
diagnosed as load sensitivity and this one may not be.

## Extent

Priced as a class, not three sightings. The population is the defect, and
CLAUDE.md already names the cost: *"a backlog of known flakes is how a genuine
red gets waved off as the usual one."* Five stories in this family have been
filed and closed as fixed, and the class is back. That recurrence is the
finding.

Case 2 (`#dispatch-model option`) is plausibly separate — a select's option set
rather than a toggle's state — and should be split out if the first
reproduction shows it failing independently of the other three.

## Last known good

None available. `browser-status` says no ancestor has ever been certified, so
there is nothing to bisect against. Establishing a first green tree is
therefore part of this story's value, not merely a precondition for it.

## Why this was not seen sooner

SH-394 moved the browser suite out of the merge gate into the release gate;
SH-418 then found that nothing ran the release gate between releases and built
`browser-watch.sh` to close it. This run is what that poller would have
reported had it been running on a timer — which SH-418 records as a bootstrap
step this repo documents rather than performs.

payload.subject: fix(release): let the pinned toolchain find its own sysroot

payload.text: Resumption decision — do not commit the staged merge against obsolete main 2d8dd34d. Current origin/main is cea6ec6d and now includes SH-567 and SH-569 as well as SH-568. SH-575 has also refuted the earlier fake-tmux contention hypothesis and establishes that clean current main passes the engine case. Abort only the unfinished merge operation, preserving every published SH-566 commit, then freshly merge current origin/main without rebasing or rewriting history. Use the full desktop-Chromium engine project on that fresh merge as the firm reproduction gate: if green, retire SH-575 as obsolete and unblock SH-566; if red, diagnose and fix it before committing. Only a tested fresh merge will be committed and pushed to existing PR 652.

Fresh-merge conflict decision — retain both feature families. The Full Auto launch modal from SH-566 coexists with current main's stop confirmation and persistent alert; live fingerprints include immutable configuration and pending lifecycle action; rendered controls show configuration, lanes, and pause/resume/stop actions. Escape is resolved strictly by topmost overlay: persistent alert refuses dismissal, then stop confirmation may close when not in flight, then launch configuration may close, then older surfaces. Keep SH-566's modal helpers and configured physical-click tests while retaining all SH-567/568/569 tests; the common real-daemon case already combines modal launch with persistent-alert acknowledgement. Keep both SH-566 and SH-569 As-built sections and replace obsolete banner prose with the current modal-alert contract. AGENTS.md and its canonical template name SH-566 as Current; HANDOFF.md remains the active SH-566 lane record rather than preserving completed SH-569 handoff prose.

Fixed and merged in PR #661 (commit edb559872, merge 78c2bde0c).

Cause confirmed by toggle, not by reading: the identical toolchain tree reports the correct sysroot when its root directory is named `tc` and the wrong one when it is named `aarch64-apple-darwin`. rustc takes the sysroot from the directory holding the librustc_driver dylib it loaded, and reads `<X>/<triple>/lib/` as the pre-built-library layout, stripping four components instead of one.

Two mechanisms shipped, neither sufficient alone:
- the toolchain now assembles at `.../$host_target/toolchain`, so the triple still keys the cache but no longer names the sysroot;
- `ensure_release_toolchain` has a single exit carrying `release_toolchain_verify_sysroot`, so the override, warm-cache and fresh-assembly doors all prove the toolchain can find itself. An empty answer is refused by name rather than resolved, because `cd ""` succeeds and stays put.

Tests derive the triples from scripts/release-targets.sh; mutation-checked in both directions. Verified end to end against the real pinned toolchain: build-release-assets.sh --check exits 0.

Standing rule recorded in CLAUDE.md.

Firm reproduction and scope decision — the fresh cea6ec6d merge fails the full desktop-Chromium engine project 1/24 at the real-daemon case after all four preceding alert tests: the lane is initially visible, but the run reaches finished before Stop-now and returns 422. The remaining 23 cases pass. This confirms SH-575 is live and order-dependent. Playwright's current official isolation contract gives each test a fresh BrowserContext/page, while test-scoped fixtures tear down after each test and worker-scoped resources last for the worker; this runner deliberately shares one daemon, seeded store, and fake-tmux state for the project. Therefore investigate shared non-browser state and teardown, not page state or locator timing. Use FULL RCA because the signature crosses browser, daemon, shell dispatch, and fake tmux and the first mechanism was already refuted. Keep SH-575 as the tracked blocker but land any contained repair in existing PR 652—no second PR—and unblock SH-566 only after the full-project RED turns GREEN.

payload.title: The Lima guest resolves its relative release cache root against $PWD, which is the read-only host-home mount, and the failure is reported as a download error

payload.description:
WHAT: `scripts/build-release-assets.sh --check` fails on the two Linux targets. Reported cause: "could not download rustc for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu from https://static.rust-lang.org/dist/2026-09-03/rustc-1.98.1-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz", preceded by "curl: (23) Failed writing body". The network is fine and the URL is correct. The real cause is two lines above it, in a message nothing treats as fatal: "mkdir: cannot create directory /Users/mikey/.cache/storyhook-release: Read-only file system".

WHERE, defect A (the cause): `scripts/release-linux.sh` passes `guest_cache_root=".cache/storyhook-release"` — a relative path — and `guest_check`/`guest_build` each normalize it with `guest_cache_root="$PWD/$guest_cache_root"`. In the guest, `limactl shell` does not start in the guest home. This checkout lives at /Volumes/Code, which Lima does not mount, so limactl falls back to the host home path, and `$PWD` is `/Users/mikey` — the host home, mounted READ-ONLY by Lima default. The guest home is `/home/mikey.guest` and is writable. Measured in the running guest: PWD=/Users/mikey, HOME=/home/mikey.guest, HOME writable.

WHERE, defect B (why it was unreadable): `storyhook::ensure_release_toolchain` (scripts/release-toolchain.sh) does not check its `mkdir -p "$download_dir" "$staging"`. `set -e` does not fire there, because every caller invokes it as `toolchain="$(ensure_release_toolchain ...)" || exit 1` and `set -e` is suppressed inside a command substitution used in an assignment with `||`. So a read-only cache root prints two mkdir errors, continues, and fails later at curl — reporting a network problem for a filesystem one. Same class as SH-576, where rustc blamed a missing rustup target for our own layout defect: a confident diagnosis pointing away from the cause.

WHEN / LAST KNOWN GOOD: introduced by 0da1b66a0 "fix(release): build artifacts from pinned local capabilities", the same commit as SH-576 and likewise after the v2.4.0 tag. The Linux half of the pinned-toolchain path has never assembled a release.

EXTENT: both Linux archives, in both phases — `--guest-check` and `--guest-build` carry identical copies of the wrong normalization. The Darwin targets are unaffected; they resolve their cache root on the host.

REPRO:
  1. bash scripts/build-release-assets.sh --check
  2. limactl shell --tty=false storyhook-release-focal-aarch64 sh -c "echo \$PWD; echo \$HOME"
     -> PWD=/Users/mikey (read-only mount), HOME=/home/mikey.guest (writable)

FIX SHAPE: a relative guest cache root resolves against `$HOME`, which is writable by definition and does not depend on where limactl chose to start; the two identical normalizations become one function. Separately, a cache root that cannot be created is refused by name, so the next such failure names the directory rather than the download.

payload.text: Commit-structure decision — preserve two-hats history even though it requires redoing the resolved merge: abort the still-uncommitted current-main merge, add the SH-575 fake-tmux liveness repair and its exact regression test as one standalone green commit on the existing PR branch, then merge current origin/main with a normal merge commit and reapply the already-recorded conflict decisions. Committing the known-red merge first would make published history non-bisectable; folding the independent harness repair into the merge commit would violate the required own-commit rule. The root defect is now directly evidenced: production asks fake tmux for the composite format '#{pane_pid}\t#{pane_current_command}\t#{pane_dead}', but the fake's first substring match returns only the command, so every periodic reconciliation parses the live pane as dead. The fix will render all three fields and derive pane_dead from the placeholder pid rather than hard-code a lie. The regression test will issue the exact production probe and fail before the repair. Static forensics replace bisect because the bug is an interaction between an older incomplete fake and a later production query, with no linear known-good tree for the exact fake-only oracle.

Regression gate RED — plugins/story/tests/test-fake-tmux-state.sh now sends the exact production engine probe. Expected '<live pid>\tclaude\t0'; the current fake returned only 'claude' and the test failed. This directly proves the parser mismatch before the repair. Implement the already-recorded fix only in the fake renderer, then rerun this test green before any merge work.

payload.title: Nothing detects a release cut outside scripts/release.sh, so a hand-cut release ships over broken code paths silently

payload.description:
WHAT: v2.4.0 was cut by hand rather than by `scripts/release.sh`. Two consequences, and neither announced itself at the time.

1. Its tag landed on the merge commit `e67be121a` instead of the VERSION-modifying commit `ab8543200`. That is the exact defect SH-494 already fixed inside the script — `scripts/release-tag-commit.sh` is intact and answers `ab8543200` correctly today — so the wrong tag proves the script was bypassed, not broken. The wrong tag is stored silently and surfaces only when the NEXT release runs `semver-cli validate` and refuses. v2.4.1 was blocked by it on 2026-09-06 and needed a tag move on a published release to clear.

2. More seriously: `release.sh` is the ONLY caller of `scripts/build-release-assets.sh --check`, which is the only thing that exercises the pinned local toolchain and the Lima guest. Skipping the script skipped that check, so commit 0da1b66a0 shipped THREE defects that made all four release archives unbuildable, and nobody knew for two days. Both were filed and fixed on 2026-09-06 (SH-576, SH-578); neither was findable by `make test`, then or now.

WHY THIS IS THE DETECTION LAYER: the rubric carve-out applies directly. This is the missing detector for two already-filed defects. `make test` structurally cannot see the release-assembly path — no Lima, no cross-compilation, no pinned toolchain — and `make test-full` adds only the browser tier. The release path is the one production surface with no automated observer at all, and the evidence is that it stayed broken across two days and one shipped release.

EXTENT / EVIDENCE:
- 0 receipts at `tier full` across 300 in this clone, so `make test-full` has never gone green here either.
- v2.3.0 tag also points at 13c4366c3, not its VERSION commit d077b0207 — so this has happened before and was cleared without being recorded.
- v2.4.0 shipped 4 assets on 2026-09-05 while the code that builds those assets could not run on this machine at all.

FIX SHAPE (to be designed, not prescribed here): something that makes a hand-cut release either impossible or loud. Candidates worth weighing against each other — a periodic exercise of `build-release-assets.sh --check` in the shape `browser-watch.sh` already has for the release test tier, so the assembly path is proven between releases rather than only during one; and/or a check that every tag matching the release pattern points at a commit that modified VERSION, which would have caught both v2.3.0 and v2.4.0 the moment they were pushed. Note the second is a detector for the SYMPTOM and the first for the CAUSE; they are not substitutes.

LAST KNOWN GOOD: v2.3.1, whose tag points at its own bump commit 053652b27, is the most recent release whose tag placement is correct.

payload.title: scripts/release.sh --bump can never complete: it bumps on a release branch, and semver-cli bump run aborts non-interactively on its own wrong_branch question

payload.description:
WHAT: `scripts/release.sh --bump <level>` aborts at the bump step, every time, on any repository whose semver `target_branch` is not the branch the script just created. Reported as: `[semver] Auto-bump aborted — manual attention needed: - open questions: wrong_branch` / `"error": "non_interactive_blocked"`, followed by the script`'s own correct refusal: `semver produced v2.4.0 but this script planned v2.4.1. Refusing to continue.`

WHERE: `scripts/release.sh`. Line ~605 does `git switch -c "release/$next_version"` — deliberately, and the comment says why: "Never on main directly: the org`'s protect-main ruleset forbids it, and the bump has to arrive through a PR like everything else." The next line then runs `semver-cli bump run "$bump" --skip-tag --non-interactive`. `bump run` is documented as "Gather then execute in one call WHEN NO QUESTIONS APPLY", and `.semver/config.yaml` sets `target_branch: main`, so gather raises `wrong_branch` on the very branch the script just created. `--non-interactive` converts that question into an abort. The two lines are individually correct and cannot both be satisfied.

The question carries no flag mapping, and `--force` does not clear it — measured: `bump gather patch` and `bump gather patch --force` both return `questions: [wrong_branch]`.

EXTENT: both bump call sites, not just the public one. The `--local-only --bump` path has the same shape and survives only because it happens to stay on whatever branch you were already on — it aborts identically from any branch that is not `main`.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE COMMAND: this is the mechanism behind SH-579. `release.sh` is the only caller of `build-release-assets.sh --check`, so a release path that cannot complete is a release path that gets bypassed, and a bypassed release is one where nothing exercises the assembly. v2.4.0 was hand-cut and shipped a wrong tag over three unbuildable-archive defects (SH-576, SH-578). This defect is the reason the hand-cutting happens; SH-579 is the reason nobody notices.

FIX: use `semver-cli bump execute`, the half of the API that means "the decision gather would ask about has already been made" — which is exactly true here, since being on a release branch is the script`'s own deliberate design. Verified on a disposable branch: `bump execute patch --skip-tag` bumped v2.4.0 -> v2.4.1, wrote the changelog entry, skipped the tag, and asked nothing. `execute` takes no `--non-interactive` flag because it never asks, so there is no hang risk to trade for this.

LAST KNOWN GOOD: none found. No release in this repository`'s recent history appears to have been produced by this script — v2.4.0 and v2.3.0 both carry tags on merge commits rather than on their VERSION commits, which `release-tag-commit.sh` (SH-494) would have prevented.

payload.title: The Lima guest build never enters the extracted source tree, and its test hides that by running from the repo root

payload.description:
WHAT: `scripts/release.sh` reaches the asset-build step and dies with `error: could not find Cargo.toml in /Users/mikey or any parent directory` (cargo exit 101), on the first Linux target it builds.

WHERE, the defect: `guest_build` in `scripts/release-linux.sh` creates `work_dir="$(mktemp -d ...)"`, extracts the source archive into it, and then invokes `"$toolchain/bin/cargo" build --locked --release --target "$target"` without ever entering that directory. Cargo resolves its manifest from the working directory, which in the guest is `/Users/mikey` — the read-only host-home mount `limactl shell` falls back to. Same family as SH-578: `$PWD` in the guest is not what the code assumed.

WHERE, the reason nothing caught it: `tests/release_targets.rs::linux_guest_build_uses_locked_cargo_and_exports_the_binary` drives the real `--guest-build` entry point, but with `.current_dir(repo_root())` — and the repository root has a `Cargo.toml`. So the fixture stood in the one directory where a missing `cd` is invisible, cargo found A manifest, and the test passed. It asserts on the logged argv, which is identical either way.

This is the SH-263/SH-364 shape stated again: the gate was right; the fixture lied to it. The test could only ever have failed if it stood somewhere production actually stands.

EXTENT: both Linux archives, the build phase only. `guest_check` is unaffected — it compiles a single probe file through absolute paths and never needs a manifest. The Darwin targets build on the host from the checkout and were never at risk.

REPRO: run `scripts/release.sh --bump patch` to the asset-build step, or invoke `bash scripts/release-linux.sh --guest-build ...` from any directory with no Cargo.toml above it.

FIX SHAPE: run cargo from the extracted tree, confined to a subshell so the surrounding absolute paths are unaffected. The test must stand where production stands — a directory with no manifest above it — and assert positively that cargo ran inside the extracted source, not merely that the command did not fail.

FOUND: cutting v2.4.1 on 2026-09-06, after SH-580 unblocked the bump step that had been failing ahead of it. This is the fourth defect in commit 0da1b66a0 (with SH-576 and SH-578) and the fifth in the release path this session.

payload.title: Restore web dispatch after a claim leaves no running agent

payload.description:
## Context

Reported after updating from v2.4.0 to v2.4.2 on 2026-09-06. Installed CLI reports story 2.4.2 (build fe688cdbe42e). The operator explicitly stopped the old daemon and started daemon 2.4.2, PID 92099, at http://psamathe.tail983f02.ts.net:3456. Last known good release is not yet established; v2.4.0 was the previous installation, not a verified good baseline.

## Problem

Starting a dispatch from the web dashboard moves the selected story to In Progress, but produces no new tmux window, no claiming comment, no apparent worktree, and no apparent agent invocation. The operator reports no visible subsequent activity. Which provider/options and whether every project is affected remain to be established from persisted dispatch history and logs.

Reproduction: open the web dashboard, choose a ready story, start a dispatch, then compare the story state and comments with tmux windows, worktrees, agent processes, and dispatch history. Use isolated fixtures for automated reproduction; do not disturb existing user stories or sessions.

Priority: critical because a supported work-allocation path leaves a persisted active state without the work being started and without a reported failure. Confirm the precise failure/reporting behavior during investigation.

## Proposed approach

Execute in --auto mode as requested. Use the RCA workflow to reproduce before changing production behavior, inspect persisted dispatch outcomes and daemon logs, test competing causes, and identify the regression origin. Inspect the shared shell dispatch/claim contract and the daemon invocation context as well as the web caller; do not assume a frontend-only defect. Existing recent changes are leads, not conclusions.

Fix the origin rather than masking the symptom with a retry or default. Sweep sibling dispatch paths. The previous release's request to skip gates does NOT apply to this fix: run new and directly impacted tests, open one PR, link it, and hand off to the centralized verifier under the repository workflow. No version bump, release, or production installation is requested here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An automated regression test reproduces the reported partial dispatch on the affected code before the fix.
- [ ] The verified root cause and regression origin are recorded durably on this story.
- [ ] Successful web dispatch creates the intended claim/comment, worktree, tmux window, and agent handoff through production behavior.
- [ ] A failed dispatch exposes actionable context and handles the claim consistently; no silent abandoned active state is presented as successful work.
- [ ] Tests cover relevant provider/auto variants and the shared dispatch failure class, without mocking away the defective production behavior.
- [ ] The fix and regression tests are committed together, impacted tests pass, and the linked PR is submitted to centralized verification.

## Out of scope

Unrelated backlog work, new dispatch features, versioning, deployment, and destructive cleanup of existing sessions or worktrees.
