The hook conflates any non-reader command mentioning a managed path with editing that path. Preserve protection against actual installed-file mutations; do not globally allow arbitrary bash commands. Read these new comments before finalizing your plan.

# SH-584: Restore reliable dispatch, Astra selection, and launcher execution

## Findings and intended result

Read-only investigation found:

| Area | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Web dispatch | Three SH-583 attempts reported success on `tmux-status-usage`; earlier successes used `default`. The recorded server is now absent. Root cause remains unverified. |
| Astra | This checkout includes Astra; the enabled Codex plugin’s catalog omits it. |
| Protection hook | Executing the installed launcher is incorrectly rejected as an artifact edit. |

Restore visible, correctly targeted agent dispatch, preserve honest failure reporting, and deliver all three fixes through one PR.

## Implementation sequence

1. **First implementation action:** run `story comment SH-584 <exact-approved-plan>`, passing this entire plan’s Markdown verbatim as one argument, excluding only the enclosing `proposed_plan` tags. Do this before changing files or running tests.
2. Begin the RCA workflow with SH-584 as the existing tracking record. Preserve the observed history and installation identities. Write failing isolated regression tests before production changes; compare competing explanations and establish the introducing commits using controlled historical revisions. Record verified findings on SH-584 and in a committed RCA report.
3. Implement the three work items below, each with its regression tests in a separate focused commit. Record each substantive decision on SH-584 before continuing.
4. Run only new and directly impacted tests. Update the mini-roadmap and handoff context. Commit, push over HTTPS, and open exactly one PR titled **“SH-584: Restore dispatch targeting, Astra propagation, and launcher execution.”**
5. Reference SH-584 and absorbed SH-583 in the PR body. Run `story link-pr SH-584 <PR-URL>`, then comment the PR link, diagnostics, and test results on SH-584.
6. Run `story move SH-584 verifying` as the **absolute last action**, then stop.

## Fixes and interface decisions

**Dispatch targeting and failure handling**

- Reproduce web dispatch with a daemon started inside an unrelated named tmux server. Compare against an ordinary daemon launch and direct interactive dispatch.
- Make daemon-owned dispatch target the default tmux server independently of inherited `TMUX`/`TMUX_PANE`; retain the project-named session. Direct interactive dispatch retains its caller’s server.
- Apply consistent targeting to daemon-owned engine and verifier paths. Operations carrying an existing cleanup lease must continue targeting that lease’s exact server.
- Verify claim comments, worktree creation, process identity, and prompt handoff independently. Repair any reproduced premature-success path at its origin.
- Preserve pre-existing claims and ambiguous handoffs. Definite failures before handoff must release only claims created by that attempt and report rollback failures explicitly.

**Astra and plugin freshness**

- Keep the provider helper as the single catalog and launch-validation source. Preserve `gpt-6-astra`, the documented identifier. [OpenAI model documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra)
- Reproduce the stale enabled-plugin condition through isolated installation fixtures. Repair refresh/verification so installation cannot report success while the enabled helper still contains stale release content.
- Keep capabilities and dispatch bound to the same enabled helper; invalidate cached capabilities when that helper changes.
- Prove selecting “GPT-6 Astra” reaches the executed provider command as `-m gpt-6-astra`. Leave the unselected model default unchanged.
- No installation changes on this machine, version changes, or release steps.

**Installed-artifact protection**

- Recognize invocation of the exact managed launcher as execution, including supported direct and Bash invocation forms.
- Inspect compound commands independently; an allowed launcher invocation must not authorize a subsequent artifact write.
- Continue rejecting actual edits, write redirections, destructive commands, interpreter code strings, and unsupported indirect execution involving managed paths. Do not allow arbitrary Bash commands.

No new public endpoint or store migration is planned. Reuse existing dispatch options, outcomes, and cleanup leases.

## Validation and autonomous defaults

- Exercise real claim/store operations, Git worktrees, shell helpers, and isolated tmux servers. Provider doubles may capture argv and supply terminal responses; they must not replace dispatch behavior.
- Cover Claude/Codex, ordinary/auto dispatch, fresh/reused claims, unrelated inherited server context, confirmed handoff, definite failure, and ambiguous submission.
- Add browser coverage from the actual capabilities endpoint through Astra selection to the launched process. Run focused dispatch browser specs and impacted Rust/plugin tests.
- Test stale-plugin refresh and hook execution/edit classification, including quoted paths, compound commands, and attempted write bypasses.
- After approval, make and document later decisions autonomously. Adopt additional findings under the operator’s context/size rule; otherwise widen SH-584 and leave it open.
- On an irresolvable hard stop, comment full diagnostics, run `story block SH-584 <reason>`, preserve the worktree, and stop.
- If verification returns work, repair the same PR with additional commits, run impacted tests, push, and make the return to `verifying` the final action.

**MIKEY ACTIONS**

1. Approve this plan, request changes, or specify another approach. Approval authorizes autonomous implementation and the single-PR verifier handoff.

Investigation execution: use focused Cargo and shell/browser targets, never the detected make test default. RCA QA reproduction tasks run as general-purpose agents because typed agents are not exposed. Three independent reproductions cover inherited tmux identity, stale enabled plugin content after successful installation, and exact launcher execution. Production files remain unchanged until the reproduction and diagnosis gates pass.

Reproduction result: real daemon + two isolated real tmux servers reports dispatch ok but selects the unrelated inherited server instead of default. Launcher regression also fails for a valid existing quoted launcher path. Decision: remove ambient TMUX/TMUX_PANE at the shared daemon helper environment boundary, retaining explicit cleanup-lease sockets and interactive helper behavior. tmux documents independent servers and explicit -S selection (https://man.openbsd.org/tmux). The observed post-claim disappearance is a context-selection defect; no evidence yet justifies changing claim rollback semantics.

payload.title: Allow proven read-only launcher operations through the installed-path guard

payload.description:
## Context

The operator explicitly requests a separate high-priority story to fix the installed-path guard and execute it autonomously. This extracts the guard work previously adopted into SH-584; coordinate with that agent and reuse any completed reproduction evidence rather than implementing competing fixes.

## Problem

On 2026-09-06 with story 2.4.2 installed, the protect-install.sh PreToolUse hook rejected executing the managed Codex launcher, including the context operation in SH-584, as an edit of an installed release artifact. The launcher simply execs story plugin run codex with its arguments, and src/plugin.rs::run_helper resolves the enabled plugin and invokes its helper. The guard treats any managed-path command whose executable is not a short reader allowlist as an artifact write. Bash execution of an approved read-only helper verb is therefore rejected before running.

Important distinction: create and dispatch are mutating operations, although they do not ordinarily edit the installed launcher. The earlier create rejection is evidence of classification behavior, not proof of a read-only operation. This requested fix must narrowly admit operations proven read-only by their actual implementation and argument contracts; do not grant all launcher subcommands permission.

Repro: send a Bash hook payload invoking the exact managed launcher with a supported read-only verb such as context or view; observe installed-artifact-edit denial. Establish exact supported verbs and flags from production code. Last known good revision is unknown; current checkout and installed hook exhibit the predicate.

## Proposed approach

Reproduce using isolated managed-path manifests and real hook entry points. Inspect the complete execution path of candidate read-only verbs (context, view, list, capabilities, ensure-cli are candidates, not a preapproved allowlist), including flags and indirect effects. Define a narrow explicit command grammar that admits only demonstrated read-only forms and preserves refusal of unknown/ambiguous operations. Keep changes in the checkout, never the installed plugin or an override file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failing automated test reproduces rejection of a supported read-only launcher operation before the fix.
- [ ] Exact supported launcher identities, invocation forms, verbs, and flags are justified from implementation evidence and tested.
- [ ] Allowed calls execute the real reader behavior without modifying managed artifacts or performing unintended domain writes; tests do not mock away classification or operation behavior.
- [ ] Mutation verbs, unknown verbs/flags, lookalike paths, shell/interpreter code strings, substitutions, write redirections, destructive commands, and mixed read/write compound commands cannot acquire permission through the new exception.
- [ ] Existing protections and supported ordinary file readers remain covered, including both relevant host payload forms.
- [ ] Error messages accurately distinguish a known write from an operation whose safety cannot be established.
- [ ] Regression tests accompany the fix; new and directly impacted suites pass. Open and link one PR, then move the story to verifying as the last action for centralized verification.

## Priority and scope

High as explicitly requested: the guard is a defective detection layer and blocks required agent read-only workflows. No blanket Bash/launcher exemption, no disabling sandboxing or hook trust, no installed-copy edits, no version bump or release. SH-584 retains web dispatch and absorbed SH-583 Astra work. Preserve its ongoing investigation artifacts; coordinate ownership of guard files and tests before editing.

Capabilities cache will include resolved helper identity/content. Hook permits only exact managed launcher direct/Bash execution, continues checking every segment and rejects multiline launcher commands conservatively (shlex is a lexer, not a full shell parser: https://docs.python.org/3/library/shlex.html). No production install or version change. Historical missing activity is not yet proven identical to the isolated server-selection failure; full helper/E2E coverage follows.

# SH-585: Admit proven read-only launcher commands

## Summary

Fix the installed-path guard’s false rejection of supported reader operations in v2.4.2. Preserve installed-artifact protection and existing file-reader behavior.

Static inspection identifies the rejecting predicate: the hook accepts six reader executables but never examines launcher verbs. SH-584 records a failing launcher reproduction and explicitly transfers guard ownership to SH-585.

## Implementation

1. **First implementation action:** run `story comment SH-585 <exact-approved-plan>`, passing this entire plan verbatim as one argument, excluding only the enclosing `proposed_plan` tags. Execute before changing files or running tests.
2. Recheck SH-584/SH-585 comments and reuse preserved reproduction evidence without modifying SH-584’s worktree. Record ownership and implementation decisions on SH-585.
3. Add a failing regression through the tracked hook, using an isolated managed-path manifest and installer-produced launcher. Confirm rejection occurs in classification, before helper execution.
4. Implement the narrow grammar below in `plugins/story/hooks/protect-install.sh`. Preserve the shell-only inert path; classification must not execute the launcher, invoke Storyhook, or contact the daemon.
5. Record evidence, supported forms, and limitations in a committed RCA report. Update the mini-roadmap and handoff context.

## Allowed command contract

Recognize only the exact absolute `$HOME/.codex/storyhook/story.sh` identity, covered by its managed manifest entry and verified against the installer’s launcher contract. Do not admit cache helpers, basename matches, path traversal, lookalikes, or symlink aliases.

Support direct shell invocation and `bash`, `/bin/bash`, or `/usr/bin/bash` followed by that launcher, with no interpreter options.

| Verb | Accepted arguments |
|---|---|
| `context` | None or one `--full` |
| `view` | Exactly one ID matching `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` |
| `list` | None |
| `capabilities` | None or one `--agent=claude` / `--agent=codex` |
| `ensure-cli` | None |

Allow one optional leading `--project <slug>` or `--project=<slug>` with a nonempty literal value. Reject duplicate options and trailing arguments.

The new exception accepts only one simple command. Reject compounds, pipelines, redirections, multiline input, substitutions, expansions, environment assignments, interpreter code strings, and wrappers. Preserve existing ordinary-reader handling separately. `shlex` supplies tokenization, not shell semantic validation; explicitly fence unsupported syntax. [Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/shlex.html)

Distinguish definite artifact writes from unproven operations in refusal messages. Retain checkout guidance and the existing override mechanism.

No public API, manifest-format, or store-schema changes.

## Validation

- Exercise Claude and Codex hook payload forms through real hook entry points.
- Execute allowed forms through the production launcher, helper, CLI, and isolated daemon/store. Assert meaningful output, unchanged managed artifacts, and unchanged domain records/events.
- Treat temporary diagnostic files and daemon runtime bookkeeping as operational effects, not domain writes.
- Cover quoted paths, project selectors, every accepted verb/flag, invalid IDs, missing arguments, unknown/duplicate flags, mutation verbs, lookalikes, symlinks, substitutions, destructive commands, and mixed read/write commands.
- Preserve editor protection, ordinary readers, missing-manifest behavior, override behavior, and the interpreter-free inert path.
- Run only new and directly impacted tests: guard regressions, relevant launcher/helper integration cases, and hook budget/bounds tests.

## Submission and autonomous defaults

Commit the fix with its regression tests; keep any adopted behavior fix in a separate commit. Record subsequent decisions before continuing, applying the user’s adoption and hard-stop rules without further questions.

Push over HTTPS and open exactly one PR titled **“fix(hooks): allow proven read-only launcher operations (SH-585)”**. Reference SH-585 and test results in its body. Run `story link-pr SH-585 <PR-URL>` and comment the PR link and final diagnostics.

Make `story move SH-585 verifying` the absolute last action, then stop. The centralized verifier owns the full suite, merge, completion, and cleanup. Returned work receives additional commits on the same PR without rewriting history.

**MIKEY ACTIONS**

1. Approve this plan, request changes, or specify another approach. Approval authorizes autonomous implementation and verifier submission.

Additional measured Astra failure within approved scope: replacing the capabilities helper during the cache TTL still returned gpt-5.6-sol instead of gpt-6-astra (new endpoint regression red). Fix keys cached values by resolved helper path and SHA-256 content, so refresh/removal invalidates immediately while unchanged helpers retain caching. Dispatch history origin traced to eb61f4d1ad2d416f1f91e86cc6333cc821147b7d (initial web dispatch inherited starter environment); 55f9c86281 later explicitly retained TMUX. This is a latent environment-sensitive defect exposed by restart, not proven introduced by v2.4.2.

The approved exception remains Codex stable-launcher only and rejects every compound command. Verify launcher bytes against the installer contract without executing it; keep helper resolution and domain reads in real integration tests. Read-only means no domain or managed-artifact writes: list creates/removes a diagnostic temporary file, and CLI reads may create daemon runtime state. Both hosts currently register Bash hook payloads; cover the shared envelope with their respective host metadata rather than inventing an unregistered native tool interface.

No arbitrary helper execution occurs during classification.

## SH-579: Make release-path failures visible

### Summary

Add an independent release observer covering remote tag placement and the real Mac/Lima preflight. Preserve the intentional ungated-release option.

Investigation confirmed that local `v2.3.0` still points at its merge commit instead of its VERSION commit. SH-580 fixed the release-script abort; SH-579’s detection gap remains.

### Implementation

1. **First implementation action:** run `story comment SH-579 '<exact approved plan>'`, posting this entire plan verbatim, including headings and numbered steps. Do this before changing files or running tests.
2. Add failing regression tests, then implement:
   - **Tag audit:** inspect every remote tag accepted by the existing release-version predicate. Peel annotated tags, verify VERSION matches the tag, and compare the target with the VERSION-changing commit in that tag’s history. Extend the existing commit resolver with an optional revision while preserving its current invocation.
   - Fetch remote tags into an observer-owned namespace in an isolated checkout. Detect changed and deleted remote tags without modifying local release tags. Report each mismatch with actual and expected commits; never repair published tags.
   - **Preflight observer:** add `make release-watch`, running one pass against fetched `origin/main` in its own checkout under the existing machine-lock mechanism. Audit tags and invoke `build-release-assets.sh --check` independently, so one failure cannot suppress the other.
   - Run preflight on every observer invocation, including unchanged trees: installed toolchains and guest state can break independently of source changes. Do not build archives, publish, install application binaries, or mint gate receipts.
3. Add `make release-status`:
   - Store atomic observation records and diagnostic logs under the shared Git directory, recording source commit/tree, timestamps, separate audit/preflight outcomes, and log locations.
   - Report missing, failed, running, stale, and successful observations explicitly. A failed newer attempt supersedes an older success; malformed records never imply success.
   - Define stale as a changed tree or an observation older than two hourly intervals. Show the exact observation age.
   - Print this status as an advisory in ordinary, changed, and full test entrypoints. Status reads perform no network access or preflight and do not change gate outcomes.
4. Provide documented hourly launchd configuration using `StartCalendarInterval` and `RunAtLoad`, with explicit executable paths and logs. The configuration must use a durable checkout, never this disposable lane. Ship and validate configuration generation; do not install a machine service from this worktree. Missing observations remain visible without scheduling.
5. Document the design and operational setup in `docs/spec/release-observer.md`; update the mini-roadmap and handoff.

### Tests and acceptance

- Real Git fixtures: correct lightweight/annotated tags; incorrect merge targets; mismatched or missing VERSION; non-commit targets; historical versions after later bumps; irrelevant tags; moved/deleted remote tags; unavailable remote.
- Observer tests: both checks execute independently; unchanged trees rerun; failures retain diagnostics; interrupted/partial writes cannot report success; concurrent passes serialize.
- Status tests: never-run, current, changed-tree, expired, running, failed, and malformed records; advisory output preserves test exit status.
- Validate launchd configuration and its durable-path requirement.
- Run only new and directly impacted tests through the targeted test runner, including `release_tagging`, `release_targets`, and `gate_tiers`, plus affected observer/Makefile contracts. Run formatting and shell syntax checks. Fixture tests must not start Lima or cut releases.

### Boundaries and submission

- This detects invalid tags and unobserved/broken preflight capability; it does not prove artifact provenance or a complete application build.
- Existing historical tag defects remain reported, not silently grandfathered or repaired.
- No Rust public API, database migration, GitHub workflow, version change, or deployment is required.
- Record subsequent decisions immediately on SH-579. Follow the requested adoption policy for additional defects.
- Commit focused changes, push without rewriting history, and open exactly one PR whose title contains **SH-579** and whose body references the story.
- Link the PR with `story link-pr SH-579 PR-URL`, then comment its URL and validation results.
- Run `story move SH-579 verifying` as the absolute last action and stop. The centralized verifier owns the full suite, merge, completion, and cleanup.

# SH-574: Detect incorrect Git identities

## Summary

Add identity checks before commit and push, plus a repository history audit. Inspection confirmed five commits with the fixture identity and legitimate history containing other authors and GitHub committers.

Use configured identities as evidence—not embedded personal addresses or fixture denylists. Keep this fix in repository tooling; do not change the installed Storyhook CLI or merge verifier.

## Implementation

1. **First action after approval:** run `story comment SH-574 <your-exact-approved-plan>`, with this complete plan supplied verbatim as one quoted argument, before changing files or running tests.
2. Record the design and investigation in `docs/spec/commit-identity.md`. Reproduce the missing detector with failing real-Git tests before implementing it.
3. Add a shared Bash-compatible helper, `scripts/git-identity.sh`, used by both hooks and the audit:
   - Derive author and committer defaults separately from global Git configuration, honoring conditional includes and role-specific settings, with `user.name`/`user.email` as fallback.
   - Read baseline configuration in an isolated subprocess so command-line configuration and inherited identity overrides cannot redefine the expected identity.
   - Compare complete name/email pairs. Missing expected identity or unreadable configuration fails with actionable diagnostics.
   - Support explicit alternatives through named Git configuration sections: `[storyhookIdentity "<label>"]` containing `name`, `email`, `role` (`author`, `committer`, or `both`), and a required `reason`. Read these from persistent global and repository-local configuration, ignoring command-scope policy overrides. Report when an alternative authorizes an operation.
4. Add `.githooks/pre-commit`:
   - Check effective author and committer using Git’s own identity resolution before creating a commit.
   - Reject mismatches, including environment overrides and `git -c` changes.
   - Preserve managed-hook chaining and propagate failures.
5. Extend pre-push enforcement:
   - Inspect actual commit metadata, independently of current configuration and receipt availability.
   - Check every outgoing commit; do not reuse the receipt report’s 50-commit cap.
   - For existing refs, inspect commits reachable from the new tip but not the advertised old tip. For new refs, exclude known destination remote-tracking history; without that baseline, inspect all reachable history.
   - Handle multiple refs, deletions, and annotated tags; skip tags targeting non-commit objects. Refuse unresolved ranges rather than silently skipping them.
   - Run identity checks even with `SKIP_PREPUSH_TESTS=1`. Preserve existing receipt behavior afterward.
6. Provide `git-identity.sh audit`, defaulting to all local refs, with an optional revision range:
   - Report raw author/committer pairs, counts, commit IDs, and policy mismatches.
   - Label mismatches as requiring review, not proven corruption. Existing contributors and historical identities are not automatically approved.
   - Return 0 for a clean audit, 1 for mismatches, and 2 for operational errors. Never alter history.
7. Document configuration, legitimate alternate authors, recovery for unpublished commits, and hook enrollment. Update the mini-roadmap and handoff.

## Validation

Use isolated fixture repositories, private Git configuration, and real commits and pushes.

| Cases | Required result |
|---|---|
| Matching global identity; matching or absent local settings | Commit and push pass |
| Wrong local name/email, role settings, environment, or `git -c` overrides | Refused |
| Corrected configuration after creating a bad commit | Push still refuses |
| Explicit alternate identity with reason | Passes with an explicit notice |
| Missing baseline; malformed approval; unreadable history | Actionable failure |
| Wrong author only; wrong committer only; unrelated cherry-pick author | Independently checked |
| Bad commit beyond position 50; multiple refs; first push; tags; deletion | Correct range handling |
| Existing bad history outside the outgoing range | Push passes; audit reports it |
| Linked worktrees, conditional includes, managed hooks | Existing behavior preserved |

Mutation-check both directions: disabling detection must fail refusal tests; rejecting everything must fail clean controls. Ensure mailmap or replacement refs cannot conceal stored identities.

Run only the new identity tests and directly impacted hook, push-gate, merge-gate fixture, and shell-contract tests. Run applicable formatting checks. Record the real repository audit without rewriting published commits.

## Decisions and submission

- This is an accidental-identity detector, not authentication. Global configuration remains a trust source; Git’s explicit hook bypass can bypass local enforcement.
- The history audit is a script because historical differences require interpretation and `story doctor` currently audits the store.
- Council execution is unavailable during planning: its skill requires “Persist the phase artifacts before advancing,” while Plan mode forbids those writes. The policy above is the autonomous fallback decision, not a council verdict.
- Record later decisions immediately on SH-574. Adopt related discoveries under the supplied context and scope rules; retain unfinished scope on the story.
- Commit focused changes, push without rewriting history, and open exactly one PR with **SH-574** in its title and body.
- Link the PR using `story link-pr SH-574 PR-URL`, then comment the PR URL, diagnostics, test results, and remaining limitations.
- Run `story move SH-574 verifying` as the absolute final action and stop. The centralized verifier owns full-suite testing, merge, completion, and cleanup.

<proposed_plan>
# SH-586 — Open Pull Request Chips

## Summary

Add compact, clickable PR chips to Web UI story cards. Each chip opens its linked, still-open GitHub pull request in a new browser tab without opening the story drawer.

```text
story_pr_links(status = open)
        │
        ▼
ReadOps::open_pr_links(project)
        │
        ▼
GET /api/repos/{id}/data
stories[].open_prs[]
        │
        ▼
populateCard()
        │
        ▼
PR #123 ↗
```

## Implementation

1. Run `story comment SH-586` with this exact approved plan block as its single comment argument. Do this before tests, file changes, or any other story mutation.
2. Add failing regression coverage first:
   - API test proving `/data` includes only still-open links in `stories[].open_prs`, omits the field when empty, and preserves multiple links in canonical store order.
   - Playwright test proving the chip appears, identifies the PR, opens its exact URL in a new tab, and does not open the story drawer.
3. At the dashboard API boundary, read `open_pr_links(project)` once, group links by story ID, and add non-empty `open_prs: PrLink[]` arrays to board story views. Do not widen `ReportData`, `story report`, or single-story PR history behavior.
4. Render one compact accent-outlined `PR #<number> ↗` chip per open link. Give it the full `owner/repo#number` in its title and accessible card label. Use an anchor with `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; stop click propagation while preserving default navigation.
5. Follow the dashboard’s established card accessibility constraint: the nested chip is pointer-operated and removed from nested tab order; the card’s accessible name announces the open PR, while the drawer’s existing PR link remains the keyboard-accessible route.
6. Keep the card render fingerprint and press-gate behavior intact so unchanged cards retain their DOM and click handlers.
7. Update the synchronized `AGENTS.md` mini-roadmap/template and replace `HANDOFF.md` with the SH-586 submission context.
8. For every implementation decision not fixed here, choose autonomously. Comment the decision and reasoning on SH-586 before continuing.

## Public Interface

- Add optional `open_prs` to each story object returned by `GET /api/repos/{project}/data`.
- Each entry reuses the existing serialized `PrLink` shape.
- Omit `open_prs` when no stored link has `status == "open"`.
- No database, CLI, `ReportData`, or single-story response changes.

## Validation and Submission

- Run only the new API test and directly impacted Web UI tests.
- Run the new Playwright spec across its configured desktop/mobile browser projects, plus targeted formatting and warning-as-error checks for changed Rust targets.
- Commit one focused `feat(web)` commit containing behavior, regression tests, and required roadmap/handoff bookkeeping.
- Push `worktree-SH-586` over HTTPS.
- Open exactly one PR; its title must contain exact ID `SH-586`, and its body must reference story SH-586.
- Run `story link-pr SH-586 <PR-URL>`, then comment the PR URL on SH-586.
- Make `story move SH-586 verifying` the absolute final action. Do not run the full suite, merge, version, release, deploy, or clean this worktree.

## Assumptions

- “Open” means the canonical stored PR-link status, maintained by StoryHook’s existing PR checker.
- Multiple open links are valid; each receives its own chip rather than silently selecting one.
- The feature applies only to board cards, not List rows or repository cards.
- The worktree is currently clean with no untracked files.

## MIKEY ACTIONS

1. Approve this plan once. Execution after approval is autonomous; no later input is required.
</proposed_plan>

# SH-321 — Automate the untrusted-origin browser proof

## Summary

Add one Chromium-only Playwright project for `http://storyhook.e2e.test:<port>`. The existing runner already creates an isolated store, daemon, seed, and teardown per project, superseding SH-321’s original concurrent-second-daemon design.

Adopt one related defect: ordinary E2E projects currently inherit an ambient `STORYHOOK_WEB_TRUSTED_HOSTS`. Fix it separately so `handoff.spec.ts` cannot silently lose locality.

## Implementation

1. Before changing files or running tests, run `story comment SH-321 '<this approved plan’s Markdown, from its title through its final assumption, verbatim>'`.
2. TDD the inherited-environment fix:
   - Add a structural regression proving ordinary projects clear `STORYHOOK_WEB_TRUSTED_HOSTS` before daemon startup.
   - Update the runner to perform that explicit clear.
   - Commit as `fix(e2e): neutralize inherited trusted hosts (SH-321)`.
3. TDD the dedicated browser leg:
   - Add project `untrusted-origin-chromium`, selecting only `untrusted-origin-cookie.spec.ts`.
   - Launch Chromium with `--host-resolver-rules=MAP storyhook.e2e.test 127.0.0.1`.
   - Exclude that spec from every general desktop/mobile project.
   - Only for this project, set `STORYHOOK_WEB_TRUSTED_HOSTS=storyhook.e2e.test`; use the fake hostname as `DASHBOARD_URL`.
   - After discovering the daemon’s port, pin `STORYHOOK_DAEMON_ADDR` to that port so the spec can stop and restart the same isolated daemon.
4. Add one browser test that starts credential-free and proves:
   - The page is genuinely non-secure and uses `storyhook.e2e.test`.
   - Pasting the named token exchanges it for an `HttpOnly` cookie and renders the dashboard.
   - Browser-observed XHR headers omit `Sec-Fetch-Site` but include `X-Storyhook`.
   - The native EventSource path succeeds with no `Sec-Fetch-Site` and a same-origin `Referer`.
   - Reload, a second tab in the same context, and a real daemon stop/start all render without another token prompt.
5. Update the `local_request` documentation to state why a proxy allowlist withdraws handoff locality and therefore requires project-level daemon isolation. Update `dashboard-authorization.md` to mark SH-319’s residual closed by SH-321, and refresh the AGENTS.md mini-roadmap.
6. Commit the browser coverage and documentation as `test(e2e): automate untrusted-origin cookie proof (SH-321)`.

## Interfaces and invariants

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| Production API | No change |
| Fake origin | `storyhook.e2e.test` |
| Playwright project | `untrusted-origin-chromium` |
| Spec ownership | The specialized project alone |
| Daemon isolation | Existing per-project store/process lifecycle |
| Restart | Same isolated store and fixed discovered port |
| Handoff protection | All ordinary projects explicitly clear the proxy allowlist |

## Tests and submission

- Baseline already verified: `cargo test --test e2e_browser_coverage` passes on the current tree.
- Install the repository-pinned E2E dependencies with `make e2e-install`.
- Run the new project only:

- Do not run `make test`, the full suite, deployment, versioning, release, merge, or cleanup.
- Push both commits without rewriting history. Open exactly one PR titled `test(e2e): automate untrusted-origin cookie proof (SH-321)`. Its body will reference SH-321, explain why `handoff.spec.ts` remains unaffected, and list focused test evidence.

Decision — regression gate: test for a durable label source, not only `getByRole(..., { name })`. Browser accessible-name computation can expose a placeholder as a fallback, so the story's suggested role/name assertion can pass while the visible prompt still disappears on entry. The new Playwright contract therefore rejects every rendered `input[placeholder]`/`textarea[placeholder]` lacking a native `<label>`, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`, and separately proves the three registration labels stay visible after typing. This follows W3C's guidance that placeholder text is a hint rather than a label replacement and kills the defect class across static modals, Settings, project deletion, and the mounted drawer.

Implementation complete on b0cfc16c4 (feature fc789407d plus current origin/main). Targeted evidence: API regression green (1/1); open-pr-chip Playwright spec green on Chromium, WebKit, mobile Chromium, and mobile WebKit (4/4); scaffold contracts green (12/12); E2E fixture hygiene green (7/7); targeted all-feature Clippy with warnings denied, cargo fmt --check, and git diff --check green. The browser toolchain initially was absent and was installed from the pinned lockfile. Sandbox-only bind refusals were rerun with loopback permission and then passed. No full suite was run.

# SH-374 — Deterministic Clipboard-Failure Fixture

## Summary

Replace the browser-dependent clipboard permission assumption with a page-local Clipboard API mock that always rejects. Re-enable all five quarantined WebKit tests without changing production behavior.

## Implementation

1. Before any file change or test, run `story comment SH-374 '<verbatim approved plan text>'`, posting this approved plan exactly.
2. Establish RED in `notice-autorepeat.spec.ts`: remove the five SH-374 WebKit skips, run the file under WebKit, and confirm those five tests fail because no durable error notices appear.
3. Add a file-local fixture that uses `page.addInitScript()` before navigation to replace `navigator.clipboard.writeText` with a rejecting async function using a `NotAllowedError` `DOMException`. Call it from `raiseDurableErrors()` so the deliberate failure is scoped to tests needing durable clipboard errors.
4. Remove obsolete `browserName` parameters, quarantine comments, and Blink-only claims. Update the dashboard-dispatch design record to state that the mutation battery now runs under Chromium and WebKit.
5. Keep production `copyText()` and shared support code unchanged. Playwright documents that init scripts run before page scripts and warns that permissions vary across browsers, supporting a deterministic API mock rather than permission-state dependence: [mock browser APIs](https://playwright.dev/docs/mock-browser-apis), [Page.addInitScript](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-add-init-script), [permission portability](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-grant-permissions).
6. For every later decision, comment on SH-374 immediately before continuing, recording the choice, alternatives, and rationale.

## Validation

# SH-353 — Bound post-merge auto-close retries

## Summary

Give `--deadline` expiry a unique machine-readable status, then stop the merge trailer loop after its first genuine expiry. Continue after ordinary story-specific failures. Preserve hook silence and successful Git completion.

## Implementation

1. First state-changing command: run `story comment SH-353 '<this approved proposed_plan block verbatim>'`. Do this before editing files or running tests.
2. Add failing regression coverage:
   - Assert an expired `--deadline` returns new exit code `12`, not shared storage/integrity code `5`.
   - Execute the installed merge hook with a recording `story` shim: exit `12` on the first move and prove later trailers are skipped.
   - Return ordinary refusal codes from the shim and prove later trailers still run.
   - Assert both paths remain silent and Git succeeds.
3. Add `AppError::DeadlineExceeded` with exit code `12`; mirror it through `WireError`, context handling, exhaustive error-contract coverage, and HTTP status mapping. Keep all existing codes unchanged.
4. In the shared post-merge/post-commit merge-arrival shell, capture each `story move` status explicitly and `break` only on `12`. Do not latch on the preceding `commit-sync`: that request may merely outlive the client while completing useful work, after which moves can succeed.
5. Update automation documentation with the complete current exit-code table, including `12` as “client deadline expired; command may still complete.” Update the mini-roadmap so SH-353 is current and SH-560 remains next.
6. Commit once as `fix(hooks): bound merge auto-close retries (SH-353)`.

## Public Interfaces

- New additive error variant: `AppError::DeadlineExceeded`.
- New additive wire error kind: `deadline_exceeded`.
- New CLI exit code: `12`, reserved specifically for `--deadline` abandonment.
- Existing human and JSON error-envelope shapes remain unchanged.

## Test and Submission Plan

- Run the new tests red before implementation, then green afterward.
- Run only directly impacted targets: `cli_deadline`, `error_contract`, `wire_envelope`, `hook_execution`, `hook_silence`, `hooks`, and `git_hook_deadlines`, plus focused affected library error/API tests.

- Make `story move SH-353 verifying` the absolute last action and stop.

## Assumptions and Decisions

- Exit code `12` is the next available project code and remains below shell-reserved command-resolution statuses. POSIX supports capturing the command status and using `break` inside the loop; Git specifies that `post-merge` cannot change the merge outcome. [POSIX shell language](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/utilities/V3_chap02.html), [Git hooks documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks)

## Summary

# SH-400 — Cancel Reclaimed-Card Removal

## Summary

Fix the dashboard race where a filtered-out card is reclaimed before its exit completes but an obsolete animation listener or 600 ms fallback later removes the live card. Preserve the current animation duration, reduced-motion behavior, keyed DOM identity, and focus recovery.

## Implementation

1. **Persist approval first:** Run `story comment SH-400 your-exact-approved-plan`, posting this complete approved plan verbatim before any file edit or test.
2. Add `e2e/specs/card-exit-reclaim.spec.ts` before production changes. Use Playwright’s frozen clock and the real search filter/render path to:
   - hide and immediately reclaim the same card node, advance through the 600 ms fallback, and prove it remains connected and visible;
   - perform multiple hidden-state renders before reclaiming, proving only one cancellable removal owns the node.
3. Run the new spec on Chromium and WebKit and require deterministic red results. Record the evidence and RCA verdict on SH-400 before editing production code.
4. In `src/web_dashboard.html`, give each exiting card one node-local cancellation handle:
   - repeated unclaimed renders reuse the existing pending exit instead of scheduling more callbacks;
   - the animation and fallback share one ownership-checked completion path;
   - reclaiming through `populateCard()` cancels the timer, detaches the animation listener, clears exit state, and invalidates queued stale callbacks before repainting;
   - genuine exits still remove the card once and retain existing focus rehoming.
5. Keep later implementation decisions durable: comment each decision and rationale on SH-400 immediately when made. Adopt only small, directly related defects that satisfy the autonomous-session limits; otherwise document them and leave SH-400 open as instructed.

## Interfaces and Tests

- No public API, wire-format, schema, or CLI changes.
- Run only the new and directly impacted browser specs on both desktop engines:

- Do not run `make test`, release, version, deployment, merge, or cleanup commands.

## Submission

- Commit the regression tests and behavior fix together as one focused `fix(dashboard): …` commit, with `SH-400` in the commit body, not its subject.
- Push `worktree-SH-400` over HTTPS.
- Confirm no existing PR targets this branch, then open exactly one PR against `main` titled `SH-400: Cancel reclaimed-card removal`; reference SH-400 in its body.
- Run `story link-pr SH-400 PR-URL`, then comment the same PR URL on SH-400.
- As the absolute last action, run `story move SH-400 verifying` and stop.

## Assumptions

- Search filtering is the preferred deterministic reproducer: it exercises the exact supported unclaim/reclaim path without fabricating `/data` snapshots or destructively changing server state. Playwright’s fake clock controls the timer boundary without wall-clock sleeps.

Decision — remove the animation listener's { once: true } option for the adopted source filter. The first green attempt correctly ignored a descendant animation, but the DOM event dispatch algorithm removes a once listener before invoking its callback; therefore the ignored child event consumed the listener and the later genuine card-exit event could not complete removal. The one-owner lifecycle already guarantees exact cleanup through releaseExit on animation, fallback, or cancellation. Registering a normal listener and removing it only in that shared teardown is the clear best-practice answer: irrelevant bubbling events leave ownership intact, the matching card-exit event removes once, and the fallback/cancel paths still detach the listener.

payload.title: PR reconciliation should not give up the verification lock

payload.description: When a story is the active / under-test Verifying story, if it needs PR reconciliation, it should not give up the verifier. Let the reconciliation run synchronously while the story holds the verifier, reconciles its pr, and then resumes verification to finish the story. Otherwise, stories can inadvertently play tag across the verifier lock and end up having to compete with each other through multiple rounds of PR-reconciliation

# SH-587 — Retain Verifier Ownership During PR Reconciliation

## Summary

SH-577 proves the defect: centralized verification returned the story twice, processed competing work, and forced two reconciliations. Keep the verifier reserved from the first conflict until that same story is resubmitted and reverified.

```text
verifying → gate → conflict → agent reconciliation → resubmission → gate → merge
                       └──── verifier remains reserved ────┘
```

## Implementation

1. **First action:** run `story comment SH-587 '<verbatim approved plan>'`, posting this entire approved plan verbatim before file changes or tests.
2. Add a verifier reconciliation reservation keyed by project and story. On merge conflict:
   - Keep the existing durable conflict comment and `in-progress` remediation handoff.
   - Notify the associated agent.
   - Retain verifier and shutdown-drain ownership while waiting for that story’s next `verifying` generation.
   - Ignore competing candidates and heartbeat/unrelated events.
   - Reverify the reserved story immediately after resubmission, regardless of current queue priority.
   - Preserve the reservation across repeated conflicts until a non-conflict outcome occurs.
3. Keep current behavior for test failures, invalid submissions, and infrastructure incidents. If notification fails before reconciliation starts, record the existing actionable `awaiting` diagnosis and release ownership instead of deadlocking the machine-wide queue.
4. Make the wait event-driven and shutdown-aware. An orderly daemon stop must release its process-local guards cleanly; no persistent lease, schema migration, busy polling, or new CLI command is required.
5. Update `AGENTS.md`, its generated template, and `HANDOFF.md` to mark SH-577 complete and SH-587 current. Preserve scaffold byte equality.

## Interfaces

- No CLI, REST, database-schema, release, or version changes.
- Extend the internal/public Rust verifier result/test seam only as needed to represent “reconciliation reserved” and target the reserved candidate’s newer verification generation.

## Tests

- First add a failing regression: a low-priority active story conflicts, a higher-priority story arrives, and the original story must be reverified first after resubmission.
- Cover repeated conflicts, unrelated wake events, generation replacement, successful merge, notification failure, orderly shutdown, unwind cleanup, and unchanged handling of red/invalid/infrastructure outcomes.
- Run only directly impacted tests:
  - `cargo test --test verification_queue`
  - `cargo test --test verification_shutdown_drain`
  - `cargo test --test scaffold --test scope_rubric`
  - Formatting and diff checks only; do not run `make test`.

## Submission

- Commit the regression and behavior fix together as one focused Conventional Commit.
- Push `worktree-SH-587`.
- Open exactly one PR titled `SH-587: Retain verifier during PR reconciliation`; reference SH-587 in its body.
- Run `story link-pr SH-587 <PR-URL>` and comment the PR link and targeted results on SH-587.
- Run `story move SH-587 verifying` as the absolute last action, then stop. Do not merge, reap, version, deploy, release, or run the full suite.

## Assumptions

- The agent’s existing `in-progress → verifying` transition is the durable reconciliation-complete signal.
- Queue priority applies when acquiring an idle verifier; it must not preempt an existing reconciliation reservation.
- Any later implementation decision or adopted defect will be recorded immediately on SH-587 with alternatives and rationale before work resumes.

Verification RED triage: the long callback list is not a set of failures; the full log marks those tests as previously PASS and not rerun. The one newly RED automated test is orphan_check::postlude_fails_when_a_survivor_outlives_sigkill. The selective rust-contracts leg waited 12s for a concurrent gate holder, then ran 260s before this single regression. No SH-328 browser or web test is reported red. I am reproducing that exact test and checking whether its time-based supervisor can expire under contention before the postlude reaches its SIGKILL verification.

Implementation decision: model reconciliation as a process-local reservation owned by the existing serialized verifier worker, not a database lease or new CLI state. The worker will preserve its activity and shutdown-drain guards across the conflict handoff, wait on the existing change bus for the same project/story to re-enter verifying with a newer generation, then run that reserved candidate before consulting queue priority. This follows the repository's established rule that active verifier ownership cannot survive its daemon process, keeps the story transition as the durable completion signal, and avoids inventing a second persisted job record beside story state. If notify cannot start remediation, keep the current awaiting diagnosis and release the reservation so an unreachable agent cannot deadlock every project.

Adopted verifier defect — orphan postlude can certify a transient empty process set. Scope: this was found only because SH-328 reached centralized verification, is small enough to finish with ample context remaining, and the scope rubric therefore favors adoption into SH-328 in its own commit rather than a new story. Diagnosis: (1) a basic SIGTERM/SIGKILL implementation regression is falsified by the exact test passing alone and all 16 orphan_check tests passing with four threads; (2) cross-worktree interference is excluded by the fixture-root process pattern, live-store classification, and in-binary scan lease; (3) the surviving hypothesis is the documented 'one true race': a time-driven external supervisor must respawn inside one unsynchronized 0.5s snapshot. The verifier exposed that false-clean path under contention. Decision: fix the detector, not only tune the test. After SIGKILL, poll for a respawn across the already-derived ORPHAN_KILL_GRACE_SECS instead of taking one snapshot. Strengthen the regression fixture with an explicit readiness handshake, parent-liveness ownership, and a delayed restart equal to half that grace: the current 0.5s snapshot then fails deterministically, while the bounded observation window catches it. This preserves loud failure for a real respawner and avoids an unbounded child. GNU Bash documents PPID/child waiting semantics, and Rust's Child documentation requires explicit child exit/wait ownership; ChildGuard remains the cleanup owner. A test-only cadence increase was rejected because this fixture already documents that tuning merely moves the threshold.

<proposed_plan>
# SH-486 — Make the SIGKILL-survivor regression deterministic

## Summary

| Finding | Conclusion |
|---|---|
| Empty stderr means the postlude found no process during its initial grace loop. | The fixture was starved; the production postlude did not miss a visible survivor. |
| SH-493 added one long-lived guarantor and documented the same failure. | The reported defect was partially repaired incidentally. |
| The remaining supervisor must respawn within 0.5 seconds after SIGKILL. | The test still contains a load-sensitive scheduling race. |
| Worktree is clean and equals `origin/main`. | Implement one focused test-only commit. |

Keep SH-486 at low priority: evidence confirms a fixture defect, not a detection-layer defect.

## Implementation

1. Before changing files or running tests, run `story comment SH-486 '<this entire approved plan verbatim>'`.
2. Harden `tests/orphan_check.rs`:
   - Retain one SIGTERM-ignoring guarantor so the pre-SIGKILL population cannot gap.
   - Replace the timed respawn loop and 600 ms startup sleep with explicit readiness synchronization.
   - Give only this test a fixture-local `pgrep` wrapper through `PATH`.
   - Delegate every lookup to the real `pgrep`; when SIGKILL empties the match set, synchronously spawn one correctly shaped replacement, wait under a named deadline derived from `ORPHAN_KILL_GRACE_SECS` until it is observable, record a marker, and return the real process result.
   - Assert the replacement marker exists, the postlude fails, and stderr names a process that survived SIGKILL.
   - Preserve bounded cleanup through `ChildGuard` and `Fixture::sweep`.
3. Do not change production orphan-check behavior or any public API.
4. Record any later technical or scope decision on SH-486 before acting on it, with alternatives and rationale.

## Verification and Submission

- Mutation-check the regression by temporarily disabling synchronized replacement; confirm the targeted test turns red, restore it, then rerun green.
- Run only:
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo clippy --test orphan_check -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo test --test orphan_check`
  - `cargo test --test timing_assertions`
  - Five consecutive runs of the exact SH-486 regression.
- Commit once as `test(orphan-check): synchronize SIGKILL survivor fixture`, including `Story: SH-486`.
- Push `worktree-SH-486` over HTTPS.
- Open exactly one PR titled `SH-486: Make SIGKILL survivor regression starvation-proof`; reference SH-486 in its body.
- Run `story link-pr SH-486 <PR-URL>`, then comment the PR URL on SH-486.
- As the absolute final action, run `story move SH-486 verifying` and stop. Do not run the full suite, merge, version, release, deploy, or clean up the worktree.

## Assumptions

- SH-493’s merged diagnosis and commit history are accepted as evidence for the original red.
- The remaining work is test-fixture hardening; `scripts/check-no-orphan-servers.sh` stays unchanged.
- If an unrelated defect appears, follow the autonomous adoption rules and record the decision on SH-486 before continuing.

## MIKEY ACTIONS

1. Approve this plan once. No later input is required.

payload.text: Decision: move ownership of the permanent `card` class to `buildCard()` by creating the node with `class: "card"`; keep `populateCard()` responsible only for forced toggles of `pending` and `not-draggable`. The first post-fix browser run exposed that the old wholesale assignment had incidentally established the base class, so removing it left new cards unselectable in both Chromium and WebKit. Construction-time assignment is the single clear owner for a class that never varies during that node’s lifetime, while render-time toggles remain the correct owner for derived state. Add this invariant to the structural regression before changing production, then rerun the focused tests.

payload.title: Improve observability

payload.description: We already have a storyhook-verifier tmux window where verifier messages are put, but let's make this into a full daily rolling log of all storyhook daemon and verifier activities. Timestamped, labeled, color-coded entries should roll by in this window as storyhook works stories through their lifecycle. This should include any stdout/stderr output from the various scripts that storyhook uses (including which script).

payload.text:
# SH-589 — Make verification progress name the actual work

## Summary

The PR #686 verification log reproduces the defect:

- `rust-suite` completed 3706/3706 tests.
- `rust-contracts` then waited more than 12 minutes for the machine-wide gate lock.
- The chip combined the current `rust-contracts` label with aggregate counts inherited from `rust-suite`, falsely reading as though Rust contracts had completed 3706/3706 tests.
- Lock acquisition, test discovery, and post-test ledger work emit no distinct progress events.

Fix both origins: publish the hidden phases and scope displayed test counts to the current step.

## Implementation

1. Before edits or tests, post this exact approved plan, excluding the `<proposed_plan>` tags, with `story comment SH-589 <exact-approved-plan>`.
2. Extend the append-only gate journal with non-checklist activity events. Activities identify their parent path, label, lifecycle status, and start time without contributing fake tests or gate legs.
3. Instrument `scripts/run-tests.sh` to report:
   - `waiting for gate lock` from before lock acquisition until the re-exec resumes.
   - `discovering tests` while resolving targets and calculating the exact denominator.
   - The existing Rust battery item during actual test execution.
   - `recording test results` while the diagnostic ledger is written.
   - Failed terminal activity before any corresponding refusal.
4. Change current-step folding so the newest active activity supersedes its running parent. When the parent test item is current, expose only that item’s exact counts; never attach counts from a previously completed suite.
5. Preserve the existing `/data` JSON field names, but correct `tests` semantics from aggregate declared counts to counts belonging to `current_step`. Omit `tests` during lock, discovery, and ledger activities.
6. Update the dashboard chip and accessible card name to render the corrected current activity and only its scoped percentage.
7. Update the verification design record and project mini-roadmap. No schema, CLI, release, or version change.

## Tests

Use red→green TDD:

- A battery blocked on another process reports `waiting for gate lock`, with no inherited test count.
- Acquisition clears that activity before discovery begins.
- Discovery reports its own activity and failure terminal state.
- Execution reports only the active battery’s exact completed/total count.
- Ledger work replaces the completed-test step until the parent leg terminates.
- Journal activities do not alter checklist contribution totals.
- `/data` exposes scoped current-step counts and omits counts for non-test activities.
- Browser chip text, live elapsed time, percentage, and accessible name match the corrected semantics.

Run only directly impacted checks:

- `cargo test -p storyhook --lib service::gate_progress::tests`
- `cargo test --test gate_lock`
- `cargo test --test verification_queue`
- `bash scripts/run-e2e.sh --project=chromium specs/verification-status.spec.ts`
- `bash scripts/run-e2e.sh --project=webkit specs/verification-status.spec.ts`
- Targeted Clippy with warnings denied, `cargo fmt --check`, `bash -n` for changed shell files, and `git diff --check`

Do not run `make test` or any release, version, deployment, merge, or reap command.

## Submission

- Record every later implementation decision on SH-589 before continuing.
- Commit one focused Conventional Commit referencing SH-589.
- Push `worktree-SH-589` over HTTPS.
- Open exactly one PR whose title contains `SH-589` and whose body references SH-589.
- Link it with `story link-pr SH-589 <PR-URL>` and comment the PR URL on SH-589.
- Run `story move SH-589 verifying` as the absolute last action, then stop.
- If an unrecoverable hard stop occurs, comment full diagnostics, run `story block SH-589 <reason>`, preserve the worktree, and stop.

## Assumptions

- The observed lock wait is expected serialization, not a lock defect; SH-589 changes its visibility only.
- Existing checklist comments retain aggregate rollups. The dashboard chip reports the actual active phase and its own test counts.
- No separate story is required for the two coupled observability faults.

## MIKEY ACTIONS

1. Approve this plan once. I will make all later decisions autonomously and record them on SH-589.

Implementation decision — represent hidden work as a separate activity record keyed by its owning checklist path, with explicit running/passed/failed lifecycle events. I weighed nested checklist items against a separate activity channel. Nested items would falsely add lock acquisition, discovery, and ledger work to ProgressItem::contribution, corrupting the established gate/test rollups. This belongs to SH-589 by the same lock/progress/verification path. The origin fix should make centralized verification acquire the gate once around make test, with inner battery acquisitions reentrant, and expose that outer acquisition as the active journal activity. Per the autonomous scope rule, I cannot establish that at least half the session context remains; I am widening SH-589 but not implementing this additional behavior now. Implementation decision — make the centralized verifier hold the machine-wide gate for the entire speculative verification command, and make machine-lock.sh own optional lock-wait activity emission. I weighed increasing the 1746-second timeout, wrapping only the production make-test call, and wrapping run_verification_gate itself. A timeout increase would mask unbounded repeated contention; a call-site-only wrapper would leave the private gate seam unable to prove the invariant. Wrapping run_verification_gate restores the documented one-wait-plus-one-run timeout model for every centralized gate invocation, while existing inner Rust battery locks become reentrant through STORYHOOK_MACHINE_LOCKS and cannot be interleaved. The lock primitive is the one layer that knows whether acquisition is pending, succeeds, or fails, so it will emit the optional waiting/acquired/failed activity; run-tests.sh will supply its parent path rather than approximating lifecycle around re-exec. No timeout increase is needed.

Implementation decision — consume STORYHOOK_GATE_PROGRESS_ACTIVITY_PATH inside machine-lock.sh before entering either the reentrant or acquired command path. Repository precedent in run-tests.sh treats progress-routing variables as boundary-scoped and removes them before nested test processes; leaving this new routing hint exported would let an unrelated nested machine-lock invocation that supplies a journal emit under the outer verifier's path. The variable therefore configures exactly one acquisition, is captured then unset, and never becomes part of the wrapped command's environment. The centralized-gate regression will assert both that gate ownership is inherited and that this routing hint is not.

Implementation complete — added non-checklist activity records and lifecycle emission for gate acquisition, Rust discovery, and result-ledger work; current-step folding and /data now attach exact test counts only to the active test item; dashboard visible and accessible text omits counts for non-test activity. Adopted timeout fix complete: verify-pr holds the machine-wide gate around the entire speculative command, inner Rust battery locks are reentrant, and the one-shot activity routing hint is consumed at the lock boundary. payload.title: `story daemon stop --force` must never fail

payload.description:
under any circumstances. It must kill any in-progress verifications and the story daemon. It must use a hard kill if necessary. All storyhook processes *MUST* stop or be killed within 2s when the force flag is used.

Without the --force flag, it should output any still-running processes (daemon, verifier, etc.) and their PIDs for diagnostic purposes.

payload.subject: chore: reconcile release preparation with main

payload.text:
<proposed_plan>
# SH-593 — Guaranteed daemon shutdown

## Summary

The verifier runs in a separate process group, but shutdown records only the daemon PID. Forced stop kills the daemon and can orphan verification. It can also fail before signaling when HTTP control or the portfile fails. The worktree additionally contains a pre-existing duplicate import that prevents compilation.

## Implementation

1. Run `story comment SH-593 '<paste this entire approved plan verbatim>'` before changing files or running tests.
2. Adopt the duplicate `PathBuf` import into SH-593 because it blocks this work in the daemon module. Remove it, verify compilation with the directly affected test target, and commit it separately.
3. Add failing lifecycle tests proving:
   - A forced stop terminates the daemon, active verifier process group, and verifier descendants within the two-second production deadline.
   - Forced stop still succeeds when shutdown HTTP is unresponsive or the portfile is missing/corrupt.
   - Stale/recycled PIDs are never signaled.
   - Ordinary stop reports each active role and PID before waiting, then still drains gracefully.
4. Add a durable, atomic, mode-0600 inventory for daemon-owned process groups. Store PID, process-group ID, role, start-time identity, and relevant verification identity. Register groups immediately after spawn and remove them through an RAII guard after reaping.
5. Write the daemon’s PID and start-time identity into its locked pidfile. Preserve compatibility with old empty pidfiles by falling back to the existing portfile.
6. Make `--force` independent of a successful control request:
   - Use one absolute two-second shutdown budget.
   - Give graceful shutdown only a derived portion of that budget.
   - Signal all identity-validated owned process groups and the daemon group.
   - Escalate survivors to `SIGKILL`, clean stale runtime files, and ledger abandoned requests.
   - Attempt every cleanup target even when an earlier diagnostic or control operation fails.
7. Keep ordinary stop non-destructive: print the daemon, verifier, and other registered process roles with PIDs immediately, request shutdown, and wait for the existing graceful drain.
8. Preserve the CLI surface: `story daemon stop [--force]` is unchanged. Extend only backward-compatible internal runtime schemas and documented Rust lifecycle types.
9. Run only directly affected checks: formatting check; lifecycle, process-group, verification-shutdown, wire/schema, and timing-policy tests. Do not run `make test`.
10. Commit the SH-593 fix and regression tests. Push without rewriting history.
11. Open exactly one PR titled `fix: guarantee forced daemon shutdown (SH-593)` with a body referencing SH-593. Run `story link-pr SH-593 <PR-URL>`, then comment the PR URL and targeted test results on SH-593.
12. Record every later autonomous decision on SH-593 before acting on it. Record any adopted discovery before fixing it in a separate commit.
13. As the absolute final action, run `story move SH-593 verifying`, then stop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `story daemon stop --force` issues all required hard-kill signals and finishes within two seconds, including during centralized verification.
- No verifier leader or descendant survives forced shutdown.
- Control-channel, store, and runtime-file failures cannot prevent best-effort forced termination of identity-validated processes.
- Ordinary stop identifies all known active processes and PIDs without abandoning them.
- PID-reuse protection prevents signaling unrelated processes.
- Existing graceful-drain and abandoned-work behavior remains intact.

## Assumptions

- “Never fail” means forced shutdown does not stop early because one control or diagnostic step failed; it still attempts every safe termination target and reports diagnostics.
- The two-second limit is one end-to-end budget, not two seconds per process or phase.
- The existing compile failure belongs in SH-593 because it is in the directly affected daemon module and blocks every regression test.

## MIKEY ACTIONS

1. Approve this plan once. After approval, execution continues autonomously with no further questions.
</proposed_plan>

<proposed_plan>
# SH-592 — Replace the absolute verification deadline

## Summary

The fixed 1,746-second wall-clock deadline terminates healthy verification after lock waits or long, progressing gates. Existing implementation is staged but uncommitted in `/private/tmp/storyhook-SH-592`; the assigned worktree is clean at `origin/main`.

## Implementation

1. Run `story comment SH-592 your-exact-approved-plan`, posting this entire approved plan verbatim before any file change or test.
2. Preserve and transfer the valid staged work into the assigned `worktree-SH-592` branch.
3. Commit the current-main duplicate `PathBuf` import repair separately. Confirm it with `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`.
4. Replace the aggregate verification deadline with a 1,746-second idle deadline renewed only by growth of the durable progress journal.
5. Require a regular, readable journal with stable device/inode identity and monotonic length. Validate it before spawn, during execution, and immediately after child exit so last-moment loss, replacement, or truncation cannot escape supervision.
6. Keep process-group `SIGTERM`/grace/`SIGKILL` cleanup. Report journal damage and idle expiration as contextual infrastructure failures.
7. Emit `lock-wait` journal records only after matching the live holder PID and recorded start time. Ignore these records in checklist folding while accepting them as supervision evidence.
8. Preserve absolute deadlines for notification and cleanup helpers. Keep `VERIFICATION_TIMEOUT` as a deprecated compatibility alias and expose the accurately named `VERIFICATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT`.
9. Update the design record and in-flight deadline documentation to state that the published duration bounds silence, not total execution.
10. For every later decision, comment on SH-592 with the options, evidence, choice, and reasoning before continuing.

## Tests

- Extend `verification_progress_timeout` for progress beyond the idle window, genuine silence, irrelevant output chatter, verified live-lock waiting, journal preparation failure, and journal loss/replacement/truncation including immediate child exit.
- Run only directly affected checks:
  - `cargo test --test verification_progress_timeout`
  - `cargo test --test verification_shutdown_drain`
  - `cargo test --test verification_queue`
  - `cargo test --test machine_lock`
  - `cargo test --lib process::tests`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- Run process-inspection tests outside the restricted sandbox if approved. Do not run `make test` or any release, version, deployment, landing, or merge command.

## Submission

- Produce two focused commits: the adopted duplicate-import build repair, then the SH-592 verification fix with regressions and documentation.
- Push without rewriting history and open exactly one PR against `main`; its title must contain `SH-592` and its body must reference SH-592.
- Run `story link-pr SH-592 PR-URL`, then comment the PR URL on SH-592.
- Run `story move SH-592 verifying` as the absolute final action and stop.

## Assumptions

- The staged prior work is the recovery source; `/private/tmp/storyhook-SH-592` remains intact until transfer is verified.
- Current `origin/main` still contains the duplicate-import regression.
- Centralized verification owns the full suite, merge, completion, and cleanup.
</proposed_plan>

<proposed_plan>
# SH-593 — Guaranteed forced daemon shutdown

## Summary

The previous agent made one valid uncommitted change: removing a duplicate `PathBuf` import that currently prevents compilation. No tests, commits, pushes, or PR exist. The branch is also three commits behind `origin/main`.

The root defect is confirmed:

- `--force` can spend five seconds on HTTP before acting.
- It then waits two seconds and kills only the daemon PID.
- Verification runs in a separate process group and survives.
- A missing or corrupt portfile prevents any signal.
- The post-signal wait can extend total shutdown beyond two seconds.

## Implementation

1. Before any git operation, file change, or test, run `story comment SH-593 '<this exact approved proposed_plan block verbatim>'`.
2. Reconcile `origin/main` into `worktree-SH-593` without rewriting history. Preserve the existing duplicate-import cleanup.
3. Adopt and separately commit the duplicate-import fix because it blocks all directly affected builds and was already documented on SH-593.
4. Add failing lifecycle tests for:
   - Forced stop killing the daemon, active verification process group, and verifier descendants.
   - Completion within one absolute two-second production budget.
   - Success when shutdown HTTP refuses, stalls, or the portfile is missing or corrupt.
   - PID/start-time mismatches never signaling unrelated processes.
   - Ordinary stop immediately reporting the daemon and active verifier roles with PIDs.
5. Add a mode-0600 daemon identity record to the locked pidfile containing PID, process-group ID, and native process start-time token. Write it immediately after claiming the lock. Read old empty pidfiles through the existing portfile fallback.
6. Add an atomic, mode-0600 registry for process groups launched by centralized verification. Record role, PID/process-group ID, native start-time identity, and verification identity immediately after spawn; remove entries through an RAII guard after the group is reaped.
7. Rework forced shutdown around one absolute two-second deadline:
   - Attempt a short bounded graceful HTTP shutdown without allowing failure to abort cleanup.
   - Read and identity-check every registered verification group and the daemon.
   - Send `SIGKILL` to remaining verified groups and the daemon before the deadline.
   - Wait only for the remaining portion of that same deadline.
   - Attempt every target even if an earlier request, signal, ledger, or file cleanup operation fails.
   - Return success after completing best-effort forced cleanup, while emitting collected diagnostics for any operation the OS refused.
8. Keep ordinary stop non-destructive and unbounded: print each known role and PID before requesting shutdown, then preserve the existing graceful drain.
9. Preserve `story daemon stop [--force]`. Keep runtime records backward-compatible and avoid breaking the public Rust return types.
10. Record every later autonomous decision on SH-593 before acting. Record any further adopted defect before fixing it in a separate commit.
11. Commit the regression tests and SH-593 implementation in focused, bisectable commits. Push without rewriting history.
12. Open exactly one PR titled `fix: guarantee forced daemon shutdown (SH-593)` with a body referencing SH-593. Run `story link-pr SH-593 <PR-URL>` and comment the PR URL plus targeted test results on SH-593.
13. As the absolute final action, run `story move SH-593 verifying`, then stop.

## Test Plan

Run only directly affected checks:

- `cargo fmt --check`
- Process-module unit tests
- `cargo test --test daemon_lifecycle`
- `cargo test --test daemon_timeouts`
- `cargo test --test verification_shutdown_drain`
- `cargo test --test verification_queue`
- `cargo test --test spawn_inventory`
- `cargo test --test timing_assertions`

Do not run `make test`, release, version, deployment, merge, completion, or cleanup commands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Forced shutdown sends every necessary hard-kill signal and returns within two seconds.
- No active verifier leader or descendant survives.
- HTTP and portfile failures cannot prevent identity-safe termination.
- PID reuse cannot target an unrelated process.
- Ordinary stop reports known process roles and PIDs before draining.
- Existing graceful shutdown and abandoned-work accounting remain intact.

## Assumptions

- “Never fail” means `--force` never exits early because one cleanup operation failed; it exhausts all safe targets and reports diagnostics.
- Safety outranks blind PID killing: a process whose identity cannot be verified is never signaled.
- The two-second requirement is one end-to-end budget, not a separate allowance for each phase or process.

## MIKEY ACTIONS

1. Approve this plan once. Execution then continues autonomously without more questions.
</proposed_plan>

<proposed_plan>
# SH-588 — Complete the Preserved Handoff-Policy Repair

## Summary

The launcher defect and adopted repairs already merged through PRs #683, #684, #685, and #689. The current worktree is clean at `origin/main`.

Complete only the valid unsubmitted work preserved in commits `9cdc6dd61` and `7c5ab9fbb`: make StoryHook comments the durable handoff record and prevent repository-root `HANDOFF.md` files from being committed. Recreate the narrow change on current `main`; do not cherry-pick obsolete merge or release content.

## Implementation

2. Add failing regression coverage that proves:
   - Generated `AGENTS.md` instructs agents to record final context in story comments and not create `HANDOFF.md`.
   - This repository has no root `HANDOFF.md` and explicitly ignores it.
3. Implement the policy:

7. Run `story move SH-588 verifying` as the absolute last action and stop.

## Interfaces

## Assumptions

## MIKEY ACTIONS

AUTONOMOUS DECISION — process-group safety. Apple kill(2) and POSIX/Linux kill(2) define a negative PID as a signal to every member of that process group. A foreground internal daemon may share its caller’s group, while the normal detached daemon and verifier explicitly create dedicated groups whose PGID equals the leader PID. I will therefore group-kill only identity-validated records with PGID == leader PID; otherwise I will signal only the exact identity-validated daemon PID. This preserves descendant cleanup without risking the invoking shell or unrelated peers.

payload.title: Improve release hygiene with github

payload.description: For the storyhook repo specifically (we won't assume this about other projects that folks might use storyhook to manage), let's create a separate `dev` branch. That is the new target branch for all PRs except for cut public releases, and the working branch from which new features are made. This way, we can cut beta releases from the tip of dev, and all future commits to main will represent stable releases.
